items.summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) flagged four high-severity vulnerabilities across select versions of Tata Motors’ iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev connected vehicle applications, which could expose credentials or enable user impersonation. Impacted apps are those at version 26.7.3 or below for iRA 2.0 and 26.7.2 or below for iRA.ev. CERT-In advised users to upgrade to the latest versions, though an email sent to Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles went unanswered.
items.title: CERT-In Flags High-Severity Vulnerabilities in Tata Motors iRA Connected Vehicle Apps

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India revised the annual coupon on its Government of India Floating Rate Bond 2034 from 6.45% to 7.26%, effective October 30, 2026, through April 29, 2027. Existing bondholders holding at face value will see six-month interest rise proportionally; on Rs 1 lakh it increases by about Rs 405 before tax. The coupon resets every six months based on Treasury Bill yields plus a spread.
items.title: RBI raises Floating Rate Bond 2034 coupon rate to 7.26%

items.summary: Former minister George Yeo bought 100,000 shares in Wilmar International at $2.97 each on Nov 4, raising his stake to just over one million shares, per a Singapore Exchange filing. His role is background: the company faces scrutiny after NEA summoned it amid transboundary haze from Indonesian fires and appointed an assessor into its links.
items.title: George Yeo Buys Wilmar Shares Amid Haze Probe

items.summary: The Call for Proposals for PyTorch Day China 2026 closes November 10 at 23:59 China Standard Time. The event takes place in Beijing on December 12, bringing together developers and researchers from across China and beyond to present session talks and lightning talks across five topic areas covering training, inference, core hardware acceleration, physical AI, and the broader PyTorch ecosystem. CFP notifications are scheduled for November 17, followed by a schedule announcement on November 18.
items.title: PyTorch Day China 2026 Opens Calls for Proposals

items.summary: Trade experts say a Democratic takeover of Congress could clarify tariffs and boost India's exports, the largest export market for the country. Bank of Baroda expects an existing trade pact to stay unchanged but flags possible tariff reviews that might help India. Indian exporters want predictable conditions; India's first-half FY27 US exports rose 11% to $50.8 billion.
items.title: India Sees Potential Trade Advantage Amid US Political Shift

items.summary: Field engineers at Databricks describe a shift toward open-weight models, citing seven pressures: weak unit economics, rapidly changing model rankings since 2023 (top intelligence ranking changed hands 20+ times), guardrails blocking legitimate work after the Hugging Face incident where GLM 5.2 replaced refused frontier analysis, evolving data-retention policies like Anthropic's 30-day minimum, governance visibility demands, harness effects on benchmarks (61.7% vs 48.1% vs 38.4%), and open-weight models now matching frontier performance at lower cost. Databricks' Unity Gateway lets teams switch models via config; average unique models per customer rose from 4.2 to 7.1, with ~40% open-weight across weeks ending January 5 and July 27, 2026. CEO Ali Ghodsi told CNBC the $3 billion July raise partly secures GPU capacity for open models.
items.title: Databricks Pushes Open-Weight Models for Enterprise AI Control

items.summary: Canada-US Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said Wednesday Canada will continue trade negotiations with the Trump administration after the US midterms, noting the new Congress takes office only in January. Speaking from Ottawa on 05 November 2026, he stressed that 'focus hasn't changed,' citing work on affordability, major projects and diversifying trade relationships.
items.title: Canada Presses Trade Talks After US Midterms

items.summary: Around 10 State Disaster Response Force personnel were feared missing after two boats allegedly capsized during a rescue operation to save stranded fishermen at Bethupalli lake in Khammam district, Telangana, on Wednesday evening. The incident occurred amid heavy rainfall from cyclone Murasu. Revenue minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy said teams had identified the possible location of the missing personnel and that they would be rescued safely, while Union minister Bandi Sanjay Kumar confirmed NDRF deployment and ongoing search efforts as officials continued rescue operations.
items.title: Telangana Officials Search for SDRF Personnel After Boats Capsize

items.summary: Pete Hegseth is increasingly seen as likely to bear responsibility for the Republican losses in the midterm elections, even though Donald Trump publicly defends him. A former senior Pentagon official told CNN that the Iran war has been a Department of War-led effort under Hegseth’s leadership. JD Vance questioned whether the conflict was worth it and said it cost Republicans control of Congress. Thomas Massie filed eight impeachment accusations against Hegseth and plans to force a House vote, while Thom Tillis warned of “a reckoning” coming as lawmakers’ strained relationship with him undermines the administration’s push for a $1.
items.title: Hegseth Faces Fallout as Republicans Lose Midterms

items.summary: Australia's oldest department store chain, David Jones, has entered voluntary administration, putting thousands of jobs at risk amid years of financial struggles and a shift toward online shopping. Its physical and online stores will keep operating while receivers FTI Consulting review the company, administrators McGrathNicol said. CEO Erica Berthold described a plan to reset the business for the future.
items.title: David Jones enters administration after nearly two centuries

items.summary: The Milburn review of youth employment will recommend that the British state create and subsidise paid jobs for thousands of disabled young people as part of an opportunity revolution to reverse labour market discrimination. Due this month, it proposes flexi-jobs alongside subsidies and skills support for 16- to 24-year-olds with disabilities or chronic illness. About a million are now Neet, nearly half (45%) disabled or ill; those young people are three times as likely to be Neet as peers. Review author Alan Milburn calls soaring numbers a moral crisis risking a lost generation.
items.title: Milburn review recommends jobs revolution for disabled young people

items.summary: Analysts expect the Bank of England to raise its base rate from 3.75% to 4% on Thursday, marking the first increase in over three years. CPI inflation reached 3.5% in the year to September 2026, up from 3.1%, driven largely by petrol and diesel costs amid the ongoing Iran war impact. The move would raise tracker mortgage repayments for around 510,000 holders while boosting savers.
items.title: Bank of England Rate Hike Anticipated Amid Rising Inflation

items.summary: Before midnight and before any official call, Republican incumbent Mike Lawler conceded to Democratic challenger Cait Conley in New York's 17th Congressional District. The seat is a district where energy costs, data center development and nuclear power shaped campaign messaging. Though climate policy was seldom named directly, Conley pledged to fight climate change as a national security priority. She carried Westchester County by a 34-point margin and flipped the seat by roughly 5 percentage points according to preliminary results Wednesday, an approximately 11-point swing toward Democrats compared with 2024. Environmental advocates say her victory opens new possibilities for clean energy investment and reversing what they call assaults on the environment.
items.title: Cait Conley Defeats Mike Lawler in New York's 17th District, Reviving Climate Hopes

items.summary: Donald Trump's defeat in the November 3 midterm elections has raised expectations of possible moderation in Washington's tariff policies, potentially benefiting trading partners like India. However, economists caution that geopolitical factors and existing trade powers may keep Indian exporters exposed to targeted restrictions.
items.title: Trump's Midterm Loss Fuels Tariff Relief Hopes Amid India Trade Risks

items.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog accepted last week's parliamentary election results as legally binding on Wednesday (Nov 4) and began consultations with party representatives to form a new government. The move followed the Oct 27 vote, in which Netanyahu's bloc lost its majority while Arab-led parties made historic gains. Israel's elections commission found no evidence of irregularities after investigating fraud claims, including unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had stolen the election possibly with foreign assistance. A Shin Bet assessment suggested possible foreign funding but offered no proof; Sohlberg called such suspicions limited in scope and warned against damaging public trust. Herzog will choose a candidate to build a coalition within several days, or Israel may hold an early next-year election if talks fail.
items.title: Herzog Accepts Election Results and Begins Coalition Talks

items.summary: S&P Global reported Japan's final services Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 51.7 in October from 51.3, marking a fifth consecutive month of expansion but falling below the flash reading of 52.0. New orders climbed for a 28th straight month on firmer domestic demand, while foreign demand stayed weak and cost pressures eased further. Business confidence weakened to its lowest since March amid inflation concerns.
items.title: Japan Services PMI Expands for Fifth Straight Month

items.summary: Democrats won historic statewide races in Texas, ending more than 30 years of Republican rule and raising prospects for environmental reform after decades under GOP leadership. Analysts point to new opportunities to safeguard data center development, lower energy costs and strengthen regulatory standards. Public anger over the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence–related data centers—which consume large amounts of electricity and disclose little water use—drove turnout, with a University of Houston survey finding nearly 80 percent of voters would support limiting such builds. New Governor Hinojosa campaigned on an immediate moratorium; industry groups responded by pledging continued community engagement while noting Texas remains attractive for investment.
items.title: Democratic Sweep in Texas Opens Environmental Reform Path

items.summary: On Halloween, Victorian Labor posted an AI-generated campaign video depicting Liberal leader Jess Wilson warning that a future Liberal government would force Australians to pay $150,000 for heart attack care. The claims were drawn from remarks Wilson made at a press conference about a $1.27bn plan to fund public elective surgeries in private hospitals. Premier Ben Carroll defended the video as her own words, but Wilson called it a smear campaign and denied Americanising Victoria's health system. Labor described the video as garbage. Experts including Clancy Moore of Transparency International Australia and Timothy Koskie at the University of Sydney say such deepfakes erode trust and call for truth-in-advertising laws.
items.title: Victorian parties clash over AI election videos of leaders

items.summary: Experts say Democrats' mid-term gains are unlikely to ease visa challenges for Indian IT firms, though they may bring tighter AI regulation and oversight. Trump remains president with executive powers over immigration. Nitin Kumar of The F* Word noted pro-regulation Democratic stances could scrutinise AI data centre bills, while Gaurav Vasu of UnearthInsight said enterprise spending shifts toward AI regardless of politics. Ritika Gupta of Aaera added that even a more predictable process may not restore H-1B reliance as firms shift to local and nearshore hiring. Among India's seven largest IT firms, H-1B approvals fell about 37 per cent in fiscal 2025 versus 2024 and roughly 70 per cent versus 2015. Policy changes may take until the second or third quarter to materialise.
items.title: US Mid-Term Elections Leave Indian IT Visa Outlook Uncertain

items.summary: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono released a statement through FC Andorra describing Wednesday as the most difficult days of his life following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus De Miguel. The two collided during Monday's match, after which De Miguel entered intensive care and died Tuesday morning. Owono said he faces questions with utmost respect but cannot think beyond Jesus and their shared pain.
items.title: Owono Speaks After Tenerife Striker Dies in Match Collision

items.summary: Singapore Post chief executive Mark Chong says the postal service will remain necessary in Singapore even as letter volumes fall with digital communication. He noted mail declined about 40% from pandemic levels to 2024 and that fewer post offices now operate than at its peak of around 60, down to roughly 40 touchpoints today. Chong firmly rejected selling the SingPost Centre in Paya Lebar, saying it is impossible to value the building while future developments may raise its worth. He plans instead to lease space for rental income and redeploy staff rather than retrench them, while transforming postboxes and introducing digital stamps as part of a shift toward convenience and cost reduction.
items.title: SingPost CEO Rejects Sale of Centre, Pledges Reinvention Amid Postal Decline

items.summary: The Nifty and Sensex have declined about 8% each so far in Samvat 2082, while the Nifty Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 fell 1.3% and 0.3%. Against this backdrop, ET has compiled 15 stock ideas from five brokerages that analysts believe are well placed to outperform in Samvat 2083.
items.title: Economic Times Lists 15 Stocks for Indian Market Rebound in Samvat 2083

items.summary: The Supreme Court said India's total fertility rate has fallen from 3 to 1.9, below the replacement level of 2.1, and that population-control laws have lost significance as their foundation had crumbled. A bench reviewing its 2003 verdict on disqualifying people with more than two children from panchayati raj elections allowed a challenged Maharashtra sarpanch to hold office and referred the matter to a larger bench. The court warned of serious consequences if demographic changes are not addressed, noting population is still rising but will soon decline toward an older profile.
items.title: Supreme Court re-examines population control laws after fertility rate falls below replacement level

items.summary: Australian data centre operator NEXTDC said its board called an aftermarket book build by Goodman Group and Digital Realty 'opportunistic', noting it received no takeover proposal. Shares jumped as much as 45.8 per cent to A$9.52, eyeing the strongest intraday gain ever after a 45.8 per cent October fall. The offer sought up to 9.9 per cent of NEXTDC in a deal worth about A$715 million ($501.14 million). The move followed an M3 Melbourne power delay and cut guidance.
items.title: NEXTDC Rejects Rival Data Centre Operators' Share Bid as Opportunistic

items.summary: Rising natural and synthetic rubber prices, driven by erratic weather and the West Asia war, are squeezing margins of India's tyre makers. Ceat and JK Tyres reported sharply lower earnings in the September quarter. Ceat CFO Kumar Subbiah said previous increases had not offset cost rises and that further hikes were planned. JK Tyres' Sanjeev Aggarwal cited a 30% rise in raw material costs over six months, while Anshuman Singhania flagged input-cost growth of 9%. Strong automaker demand gives makers room to pass on higher costs.
items.title: Indian tyre makers consider price hikes as rubber costs surge

items.summary: The Spirit of Tasmania IV reached Geelong four hours late after identifying a fault and requiring a tugboat escort through Port Phillip Bay. TT-Line said the Master identified the fault as the vessel prepared to transit Port Phillip Heads on Thursday morning, with the tug travelling from Geelong causing the delay; no further details have been released while technicians diagnose the issue. Separately, the Australian Transport Safety Bureau is investigating a steering incident involving sister ferry Spirit V during a trial voyage on October 26 off Point Henry, where slow autopilot response led to heading oscillations before control was regained. A final report is expected in the second quarter of next year.
items.title: Spirit of Tasmania IV delayed by fault; ATSB probes sister ferry steering

items.summary: After Democratic candidates won Tuesday’s state and congressional races across much of the country, including Texas—a national data center hotspot—some in the tech industry turned to building compute in orbit. Elon Musk posted that “data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” while Jordan Lasker called them an “incredible idea.” Companies such as Google, SpaceX—which aims to deploy thousands of AI satellites by late 2027—and Blue Origin—already seeking a permit for up to 50,000 satellites—are moving forward. Experts caution that space-based centers are costlier and harder to scale, while Texas’s split government may limit near-term policy changes.
items.title: Democratic wins push tech figures toward space data centers

items.summary: The Associated Press produced swing maps comparing this week's midterm Senate results to the 2024 presidential vote, showing a sharp Democratic shift across many counties. Democrats flipped seven seats, including three held by Republicans for decades — Texas, South Carolina and Kansas. Obama and Trump agreed candidate quality was crucial.
items.title: Swing Maps Reveal Sharp Blue Wave in Senate Midterms

items.summary: Canary Media reports that Democrats won major national and state races in Tuesday's midterm elections, positioning clean energy for gains through Democratic control of legislatures, governorships, utility commissions, and ballot measures. In Michigan, where Democrats hold a trifecta after 2022, leaders may pass additional ambitious climate measures despite an earlier attempt to repeal the existing target of 100% clean energy by 2040. Similar opportunities exist in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Nevada, Arizona, and Georgia's Public Service Commission — where Democrats now hold a 3–2 majority after spending helped promote their candidates. Utility boards in several other states stayed Republican or remain uncalled as of Wednesday afternoon. Voters also approved clean energy ballot proposals in three states, including an Oregon tax on corporations to fund climate projects, while Michigan voters rejected rules that would let utilities sidestep campaign-finance limits.
items.title: Clean Energy Wins from Midterm Elections

items.summary: President Donald Trump, who campaigned promising regime change in Iran, instead lost control of Congress as voters frustrated by the war and rising fuel prices backed Democrats. Analysts describe a weakened president now weighing either a negotiated exit from the conflict or riskier escalation.
items.title: Trump's Defeats at Home Force Iran Policy Choice

items.summary: Voters in Piqua and Trenton, Ohio approved bans on large data centers, recalling commissioners who supported Meta's project and blocking Amazon's proposed campus. Outside Columbus, Ashville repealed its deal with EdgeConneX amid nationwide ballot measures against such facilities. Analysts note over 40% of planned US capacity sits in states with pauses, though buildout continues as hyperscaler stocks rose.
items.title: Ohio Voters Reject Data Center Projects, Pressuring Tech Firms

items.summary: Authorities in Yemen's Taiz province recorded 5,025 illness cases in October, linking them to accumulating waste as fighting displaced thousands of families. The Office for Siege Affairs cited infectious and respiratory illnesses amid garbage piled up across the city. Deputy health governor Aziz Ahmadi accused Houthi forces of blocking waste trucks from reaching a temporary landfill west of Taiz city, where 6,400 families have sought refuge. Governor Nabil Shamsan said arrivals pushed displaced families to 39,400. The Houthis did not comment on the shelling that killed three girls and a woman in Al-Athawir village.
items.title: Taiz Province Records Over 5,000 Illness Cases Amid Fighting

items.summary: Atharva Kirti Sagar, a four-year-old from Bengaluru, earned recognition from the India Book of Records for reading 1,676 English words from ‘A Send-off Party’ in The Magic of the Lost Temple by Sudha Murty. He completed it in 26 minutes, 49 seconds and 76 milliseconds on September 7, 2026, aged four years, 11 months and 10 days. The entry lists him under ‘Maximum English words read from a story book by a kid’ and places him in the Young Achievers category.
items.title: Four-Year-Old Bengaluru Boy Sets Reading Record Under Half an Hour

items.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term on 25 October 2026, taking 51.79% of valid votes against Flávio Bolsonaro’s 48.21%. Three weeks earlier the far-right candidate led with 47.03% to Lula’s 45.16%, so the result reflected a campaign mobilization rather than momentum. A National Confederation of Commerce July 2026 survey found 82% of families had debts, and debt payments reached about 29.5% of income. The victory drew on street and digital organizing plus a broad anti-authoritarian front; analysts now weigh whether Lula can sustain social spending amid a benchmark interest rate of 13.75% set in September 2026 and the resilience of Bolsonarismo, public security concerns, and trade negotiations with the Trump administration.
items.title: Lula’s Narrow Runoff Victory and Brazil’s Democratic Realignment

items.summary: Voters in recent elections largely backed candidates and measures restricting AI and data centers nationwide. Redbud Consulting reported that 38 of 44 ballot measures seeking to limit data centers passed across 10 states so far. Analysts say the rules mainly affect projects planned for 2028, not those already built or approved through 2027. Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governor race Axios said could disrupt Trump’s buildout plans; Bloomberg reported about 41 percent of expected 2028 capacity is in Texas and roughly 13 gigawatts are now exposed.
items.title: Big Tech blames voter AI backlash on anti-Trump sentiment, not opposition to technology

items.summary: President Donald Trump is considering whether to keep Pete Hegseth as defence secretary following Republican defeats in the midterms, with CBS News citing sources on internal discussions possibly influenced by the Iran war. VP JD Vance linked the conflict to the defeat, while White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly affirmed full confidence in Hegseth and dismissed replacement talks involving Ron DeSantis.
items.title: Trump weighs replacing Hegseth after GOP midterm losses

items.summary: US AI and data centre stocks fell after Democrats won key midterms, putting electricity costs and job losses in focus. CoreWeave, Iren, Nebius, GE Vernova, Vertiv, Nvidia and Marvell all slipped even as the Nasdaq 100 rose more than 1%. Analysts say political pressure may slow data centre expansion but is unlikely to derail AI development; one strategist called the concern overblown. Others warn of higher production costs, red tape and a tougher year-end rally in midterm years. The article notes investors were already questioning whether debt-fuelled spending can be sustained (The Economic Times).
items.title: AI Stocks Retreat Amid Democratic Midterm Sweep

items.summary: World leaders gathered Wednesday evening at Madrid's Teatro Real as King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia inaugurated the 30th Ibero-American Summit. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez greeted delegations from the 22-member community, though only 10 countries were represented by their heads of state or government. The absence of Brazil, Mexico and Venezuela highlighted political divisions ahead of Spain's general election on 29 November.
items.title: Madrid Opens Ibero-American Summit Amid Political Divisions

items.summary: In a Guardian US column, Robert Reich argues that Tuesday's midterm results were not the expected swing against the party in power but rather the surge of anti-establishment populism. He contends inflation is controlled and unemployment low, so voters' anger stems from corporations, mega donors and big tech billionaires. Reich notes this sentiment propelled Trump to office before he became part of the establishment, prompting many supporters to abandon him over crony capitalism. A CNBC poll placed corruption as the top voter concern, while Democratic candidates campaigned on issues like datacenter costs and campaign finance reform.
items.title: Robert Reich Attributes Midterm Results To Anti-Establishment Populism

items.summary: An author argues that Fifa has already exceeded its own revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn. Per reporting from the Times, a third of that total—$5bn—came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, which would make direct fan income five times higher than at Qatar's 2022 tournament, when it stood at $929m. The piece frames this as proof Fifa was right about money but wrong about enjoyment. Attendance reached 6.8 million versus a prior record of just under 3.6 million in the United States in 1994. The author concludes that reforming Fifa depends on slowing its money stream, and notes Infantino may survive fallout from selling commercial rights to private equity as his March election approaches.
items.title: Fifa's World Cup Revenue Confirms Its Priorities

items.summary: For the first time, Volvo CE electric equipment is being used in the National Wildlife Refuge System. A battery-powered ECR25 compact excavator and L25 wheel loader are building an ADA-accessible trail at Virginia’s Occoquan Bay refuge to reduce diesel exhaust and noise on wildlife. Dr. Ray Gallant of Volvo CE said the project shows how electric machines can support a climate-friendly construction future.
items.title: Volvo CE Deploys Electric Equipment in National Wildlife Refuge

items.summary: The family of slain Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Pradeep Purnekar approached the Bombay High Court seeking a court-monitored, independent murder investigation. Alleging lapses by the 23-member Special Investigation Team after 35 days and five arrests, they claim evidence was suppressed, phones recovered before registration, and eyewitness confidentiality breached. The petition was posted for hearing on December 5; Thane Police Commissioner Ashutosh Dumbare maintains the probe is progressing.
items.title: Purnekar Family Seeks Court-Monitored Murder Probe in Bombay High Court

items.summary: The US Treasury sanctioned India-based Suniel Kumar Sharma and his spouse Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, along with several associated companies, for allegedly helping sanctioned vessels transport Iranian petroleum through fraudulent maritime registrations. Announced by Secretary Scott Bessent on August 24, 2026 under Executive Order 13902, the measures block their property and prohibit transactions. The Treasury also separately designated Türkiye-based Fugo Ground Services Inc for servicing Iranian airlines.
items.title: US Sanctions Indian Couple Over Iran Shadow Fleet Role

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in Madrid on Wednesday, keeping his visit secret until he landed. He will meet Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, King Felipe VI and several international leaders during the 30th Ibero-American Summit over two days. The summit coincides with a rightward shift among Latin American presidents, including Javier Milei of Argentina and José Antonio Kast of Chile, while leftist allies such as Claudia Sheinbaum and Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva are absent. Zelensky says strengthening Ukraine's air defences remains the top priority.
items.title: Zelensky Visits Madrid for Ibero-American Summit Talks with Sánchez and Latin American Leaders

items.summary: Brent crude fell $9.27, or 8.9%, to $94.29 a barrel on US midterm results, its lowest since September 4; WTI dropped $7.44, or 7.8%, to $88.54. Executives say Trump may now let prices rise while pursuing military goals against Iran, though escalation could disrupt supplies further. Brent is near $100 a barrel and freight costs are several times higher than before the war.
items.title: Crude Prices Fall as Iran War Risks Linger After Midterms

items.summary: Voters in this year's midterms signaled strong opposition to data centers, even though the issue was rarely on ballots directly. Candidates who called for limiting development won competitive races in Georgia, Ohio, and Texas; at least 40 local ballot initiatives addressed curbing such projects, with roughly half concentrated in Ohio alone (per Ballotpedia), of which about 24 have been officially approved as results were still being tabulated. Opinion surveys show growing public concern, including overwhelming majorities of Ohioans who said data centers harm the environment and quality of life, and nearly eight in ten favoring a temporary ban on new facilities.
items.title: Midterm Voters Rebuke Data Center Boom

items.summary: The FDA granted tentative approval of a generic lenacapavir, a twice-a-year injection that helps prevent HIV infection. The Associated Press reported the drug will cost $40 per person a year in 120 low- and middle-income countries. Approval follows Western aid cuts to African HIV-prevention programs, which sparked fears of hundreds of thousands of additional AIDS deaths. A global health advocate said a large-scale rollout could help bring an end to the HIV epidemic.
items.title: FDA grants tentative approval of low-cost HIV injection

items.summary: Political groups backing and opposing the AI industry spent millions influencing Tuesday’s midterms with mixed outcomes, as some heavily backed candidates lost while others won. Analysts note it is hard to separate this spending from the broader Democratic wave that swept many races. Groups like Leading the Future favor a national AI framework and plan continued 2028 spending; Guardrails Alliance aims to make AI money politically toxic.
items.title: AI PAC Spending Yields Mixed Results in Midterms

items.summary: Farmers in Maharashtra intensified a sugarcane-price agitation by blocking the Pune-Bengaluru highway for a second day, demanding a first instalment of Rs 4,500 per tonne. Led by Raju Shetti's Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana, thousands continued an indefinite blockade near the Kini toll plaza while threatening to disrupt milk and vegetable supplies to Mumbai and Pune if talks fail. The group accused sugar mills of withholding fair prices despite strong earnings from sugar, ethanol, bagasse and molasses. Traffic diversions were arranged across western Maharashtra as truck drivers staged a separate protest against police force. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis appealed for the agitation to end peacefully amid ongoing government discussions.
items.title: Maharashtra Farmers Threaten Milk and Vegetable Supply Cuts Over Sugarcane Prices

items.summary: Global butane prices are surging, with Northwest European November prices reaching $1,125/t by early November—their highest in 30 years. Asian and US Belvieu prices also hit records at $1,180/t and $920/t respectively. The surge stems from a reorientation of propane/butane trade flows since the March US-Iran war: Gulf exports to Asia collapsed while US share rose to 65%. Seasonal winter blending demand further tightens supplies as American cargoes leave Europe short, with ARA imports falling to 130,000 tonnes. India faced severe LPG shortages after imports dropped from 2.03 million tonnes in February to 1.17 million tonnes in March—a fall of more than 40%. The article notes relief depends on Gulf recovery and maritime security in the Hormuz Strait.
items.title: Butane Prices Hit Decade Highs Amid US Supply Shift

items.summary: South Sudan hosts what is called the world’s largest mammal migration, involving roughly 6 million antelopes moving across seasonal swamps and grassland. A new “lines of life” map joins millions of points from GPS collars on 262 migratory animals since 2023 to show their movements. The routes mostly fall outside Boma and Badingilo national parks, which together cover at least 70% of the time the antelopes spend beyond park boundaries. African Parks produced the map; its manager Inge van den Meiracker says it helps identify high-use corridors and mating grounds. A 2025 aerial survey estimates populations including about 5.17 million white-eared kob, though figures are not exact counts.
items.title: A GPS map charts South Sudan’s antelope migration

items.summary: Clément Delangue, Hugging Face’s CEO, said Wednesday at WIRED World Fair in Miami that future AI risks most likely come from large companies building secretly while open models defend. He described his probability of human extinction as ‘close to zero,’ contrasting with researchers warning of existential danger. Nvidia announced a $12.93 billion acquisition this September; Hugging Face reported around 18 million users and now more than 20 million AI builders.
items.title: Hugging Face CEO Downplays AI Doom Risk

items.summary: General Motors recalled more than 67,000 Cadillac and Chevy electric vehicles after a software glitch in the brake system control module could cause temporary loss of braking. The issue followed an April 10, 2026 report from GM’s Speak Up for Safety program; internal testing replicated it. Affected models include certain Cadillac Lyriq, Celestiq, Vistiq and Chevy Blazer EV. Owners will receive free over-the-air updates, with letters expected by December 14, 2026.
items.title: GM Recalls Over 67,000 EVs Over Brake Software Glitch

items.summary: Nothing, the smartphone startup behind Nothing Phone, says it is developing an AI product whose nature remains unclear. On Wednesday, CEO Carl Pei posted on X that its first “AI-native product” ships in December. He described it as a tool with no new screen and not an app, while downplaying links to AI wearables such as smart glasses the company has also teased.
items.title: Nothing CEO Carl Pei hints at December AI device

items.summary: Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia inaugurated the 30th Ibero-American Summit at Madrid's Teatro Real on Wednesday evening, with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez greeting delegations from the 22-member bloc. Only 10 countries sent heads of state or government; absent leaders included Brazil's Lula da Silva, Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum and Venezuela's Delcy Rodríguez, highlighting divisions ahead of Spain's general election on 29 November.
items.title: Madrid Opens Ibero-American Summit Amid Low Attendance

items.summary: On Tuesday, Chadian President Mahamat Idriss Deby Itno met with Algerian Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf at the presidential palace in N'Djamena. The two discussed strengthening bilateral cooperation and implementing agreements signed during Deby's earlier visit to Algiers. Attaf said Chad and Algeria share common goals for regional prosperity.
items.title: Chadian President Meets Algerian Foreign Minister in N'Djamena

items.summary: After the Iran war and closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted its exports, QatarEnergy is becoming the largest buyer of liquefied natural gas from the United States through two new agreements. The firm said Iranian missile attacks in March took out 17% of export capacity and caused an estimated $20 billion annual revenue loss. It declared force majeure on some long-term contracts for up to five years, extending it another month into December 2026. QatarEnergy signed deals with Cheniere for up to 4 million tons per annum from Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi through 2054, and with Woodside Energy for 3 million tons per annum starting in 2030. CEO Al-Kaabi said the purchases strengthen its position amid a global gas crunch the IEA warns could last into 2027. He noted Qatar is ready to resume normal operations within weeks of Hormuz reopening, though only a few ships are currently passing through.
items.title: Qatar Signs Long-Term U.S. LNG Purchase Deals After Hormuz Crisis

items.summary: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono says he is living through 'the most difficult days of my life' after Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel died from a serious injury in a collision with him during a Spanish second division match on Monday. Police opened a routine manslaughter inquiry, and both clubs postponed weekend matches while mourning the father-of-one.
items.title: Keeper Owono Calls It His Most Difficult Days After De Miguel's Death

items.summary: At a Democratic victory rally, Abdul El-Sayed greeted Vice-President JD Vance with 'JD [Vance], habibi,' before introducing himself as the first Muslim senator-elect. He rejected accusations from conservative media and President Trump that he supported the Muslim Brotherhood. The article notes several other politicians with African roots also won in this year's midterms: Melat Kiros, 29, became the first Gen Z woman elected to Congress; Adrian Boafo will represent Maryland's 5th District after Steny Hoyer retired; Ilhan Omar, 44, won a fifth term despite an ongoing federal investigation into her immigration paperwork. Others broke through in state and local politics: Junior Ezeonu at 27 and Carol Kazeem, 34. Their victories have inspired young African voters ahead of elections due in Nigeria and Kenya in 2027.
items.title: African-American politicians make history in US midterms

items.summary: On November 4, 2026, a three-judge Supreme Court Bench recalled paragraphs 1 to 3 of its November 3 order against Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation Commissioner Ashwini Bhide. Senior advocate R. P. Bhatt argued the civic body had complied with earlier directions dated November 13, 2025 and July 28, 2026. The Bench withdrew observations on wilful disobedience, a show-cause notice, and salary restraint, while clarifying it held no opinion on compliance. Commissioner Bhide was directed to file a personal affidavit before the next hearing; paragraphs 5 and 6 remain undisturbed.
items.title: Supreme Court Recalls Wilful Disobedience Order Against Mumbai Commissioner

items.summary: The South Region Cyber Police arrested Pushpa Bind, a computer engineer, on November 3 in connection with allegedly hacking an investor's Demat account and selling shares worth Rs 4.58 crore before buying penny stocks valued at just Rs 1.71 crore. Police allege she used her technical knowledge to access the victim's accounts through a SIM swap linked to their email address. A team led by Senior Police Inspector Nandkumar Gopale froze shares worth Rs 2.86 crore, and Bind faces three other cases from 2025 plus one registered this year. Further investigation continues into whether additional investors were targeted.
items.title: Mumbai Police Arrest Woman for Alleged ₹4.58 Crore Demat Account Fraud via SIM Swap

items.summary: On 3 November, ahead of the Belém summit, the Brazilian presidency of COP30 released a voluntary “deforestation roadmap” outside the talks’ official agenda. By its end, 93 countries had signed on to develop pathways to reverse forest loss and degradation by 2030 – short of the 196 parties needed for consensus, so it is not a formal outcome. COP30 president André Corrêa do Lago said the presidency would work towards both deforestation and fossil-fuel phaseout roadmaps outside the process. The roadmap makes no new commitments; its objective is to translate existing forest outcomes into coordinated action across national efforts, international architecture and finance. It identifies 18 policies countries can use. Kelly Stone of Climate Land Ambition and Rights Alliance said the commitments must become “actual urgent action on the ground.” Some countries declined to sign: India objected over trade links; Russia opposed a universal roadmap as not mandated under existing agreements.
items.title: Brazil’s COP30 Presidency Releases Voluntary Deforestation Roadmap

items.summary: Elon Musk spent at least $446m backing Republicans in the US midterm elections, more than his nearly $290m total in 2024. Democrats won every Senate race where America Pac invested heavily and took control of Texas. Talarico said all the money was no match for voters. The spending may end an era of lax regulation benefiting Musk's companies as Democratic officials vow scrutiny.
items.title: Musk's Record Midterm Spending Backed by Democratic Gains

items.summary: At a Wall Street Journal tech conference in Napa, California on Wednesday, OpenAI President Greg Brockman said the company now earns most of its revenue from enterprise sales and expects to be ready for an initial public offering in 2027. He responded "I think so" when asked about next year's timeline. Reuters reported that San Francisco-based OpenAI has been accelerating fundraising after delaying its IPO plans, while competing with Anthropic over Codex.
items.title: OpenAI President Brockman Signals IPO Readiness for 2027 Amid Enterprise Growth

items.summary: A group of Indian-origin executives now heads major global companies, with Narayen's roughly 19-year tenure since 2007 the longest among them. No official list exists, so counts vary by publication and definition. The most watched transition is at Adobe: Anil Chakravarthy becomes president and CEO on 1 December 2026, succeeding Shantanu Narayen as executive chair. Other recent changes include P&G's Shailesh Jejurikar, Microsoft Gaming's Asha Sharma, and Meta naming Kunal Shah head of WhatsApp alongside a $900 million CRED investment.
items.title: Indian-Origin CEOs Lead Global Firms as Adobe Prepares Leadership Handover

items.summary: Bloomberg reported Wednesday that Apple is reducing the daily amount its engineering teams can spend on AI, a significant shift from a company known for integrating the technology into workflows. In October, Apple lowered the cap from $300 to $200 per day, with further cuts planned down to $100 and possibly as low as $25 outside engineering. The move follows concerns about token costs outweighing unclear productivity gains.
items.title: Apple reportedly cutting internal AI spending caps amid token cost concerns

items.summary: Alphabet's Google confirmed to Reuters that it began offering voluntary exit packages in June, expanding the program globally across Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland. The move comes amid rising artificial intelligence spending that has pressured Alphabet's stock price. A spokesperson said some teams introduced a voluntary exit program with severance this year.
items.title: Google Expands Voluntary Exit Offers Across Five Countries Amid AI Spending

items.summary: Visa announced six global tech hubs at a new Paya Lebar centre, bringing some 1,500 staff working on agentic AI, next-generation payments and trusted commerce. The firm said the technologies will be deployed across its global network. Visa's president for technology Rajat Taneja called it an extraordinary period of commerce innovation driven by AI and digital money.
items.title: Visa Opens Six Tech Hubs in Singapore

items.summary: Australia’s oldest department store, David Jones, collapsed on Nov 5 after almost 200 years in business. McGrathNicol executives were appointed voluntary administrators while FTI Consulting staff became receivers; the chain keeps trading as administrators seek buyers to recapitalise it. Anchorage Capital Partners had bought the retailer in 2023. Receiver Christopher Hill cited rising costs, an outdated footprint and supply-chain challenges, while chief executive Erica Berchtold said the company has a plan to reset for the future.
items.title: David Jones Collapses After Nearly Two Centuries

items.summary: Opinion writer Courtney C. Radsch argues that the Democratic victories in the House, Senate and state offices signal a voter mandate to confront corporate power and what she calls technofascism. She frames tech accountability—AI governance, monopoly break-ups, media plurality—as central to this agenda, pointing to growing state-level limits on AI products as evidence of popular will. Radsch urges the incoming Congress to use hearings, subpoenas and floor control to hold executives accountable, citing reports that Meta interfered in elections in the US and Brazil. She acknowledges legislative constraints like the Senate filibuster and presidential veto but insists oversight should continue regardless.
items.title: New Congress Faces Test on Big Tech Power After Voter Mandate

items.summary: Databricks announces Apache Spark 4.3, which brings stateful processing to its low-latency Real-Time Mode in Structured Streaming. The release claims sub-150 ms P99 end-to-end latency across three representative benchmarks for streaming aggregation, deduplication, and custom stateful operations. These figures are measurements of the tested workloads rather than a guarantee for every pipeline. Spark 4.3 also introduces native concurrent stage scheduling and pipelined shuffles to support continuous data flow between long-running tasks. The version marks the start of a quarterly release cadence instead of one every six months, with Databricks Runtime availability noted separately in its own release notes.
items.title: Apache Spark 4.3 Adds Stateful Real-Time Processing and Faster Releases

items.summary: The government relaxed key terms in its effort to procure 10,000 fresh GPUs under the IndiaAI Mission. Providers can now qualify with a minimum capacity of 512 GPUs or TPUs at one Indian data centre location, down from 1,000 earlier. The first stage covers technical qualification only; bidders need not submit a financial bid or commit to service levels. The minimum qualifying score fell to 60 out of 100 from 75 under the prior framework.
items.title: IndiaAI GPU procurement eases entry, price pain persists

items.summary: Ravi Uppal, a prime accused in the multi-crore Mahadev online betting case, was arrested by Dubai police. Enforcement authorities have formally moved for his extradition and sources say he is likely to be handed over soon. India had requested his return after learning of the arrest; agencies again located him in May this year. Uppal helped launch the app in 2019 and franchised thousands of branches on a profit-sharing basis.
items.title: India Seeks Extradition of Mahadev Betting Accused Held in Dubai

items.summary: Guardian Australia reports that Beau Lamarre-Condon, a 31-year-old police officer accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his service weapon at their Paddington home on 19 February 2024, gave testimony during the high-profile Sydney trial. He told the court he was transferred to the youth command division to escape officers tormenting him at Surry Hills station, described remembering 12 to 15 graphic incidents as an officer, and recounted a co-worker who shot himself in the head while off duty.
items.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon gives evidence in double murder trial

items.summary: On Election Day, California voters rejected Proposition 45, a measure backed by the state Chamber of Commerce that would have sped environmental review under CEQA. As of Wednesday afternoon with more than half the ballots counted, just over 54 percent opposed it and about 46 percent supported it; nonpartisan Public Policy Institute polling showed support falling from 73 percent to 46 percent between July and October. No on Prop 45 spokesperson Woody Little said millions voted to defend core environmental protections. Elsewhere, Colorado voters rejected Amendment 82 protecting natural gas sales, while Arizona and Texas measures touched utilities and water fees. The outcome reflected broad voter support for safeguarding the environment amid concerns over housing, energy costs and climate goals.
items.title: California Voters Reject Environmental Law Overhaul

items.summary: Sources said Wednesday that Mitsui Chemicals is considering acquiring semiconductor materials maker JSR in a possible deal worth over ¥1 trillion, which could become Japan’s largest chemical-industry acquisition. The company stated it is examining options to improve corporate value and strengthen its semiconductor business. Shares would be bought from parent fund Japan Investment Corporation (JIC), which took JSR private for about ¥900 billion in 2024.
items.title: Mitsui Chemicals Weighs Over ¥1 Trillion Bid for JSR

items.summary: On an election day, the Alabama Public Service Commission voted to request that Alabama Power voluntarily stop billing customers for advertising costs immediately, rather than waiting until a new law takes effect in 2029. The utility spends more than $6 million annually on general advertising, roughly $4 per customer according to federal filings. President Cynthia Lee Almond moved the measure; commissioners Jeremy Oden and Chris Beeker IV voted yes. Energy Alabama's Daniel Tait praised the action as strong customer protection. Alabama Power did not respond to a request for comment. The vote comes amid criticism of rising electricity prices ahead of a commission overhaul in January.
items.title: Alabama Regulators Seek Immediate End to Utility Advertising Fees

items.summary: On Wednesday, Hungary released communist-era secret police files identifying tens of thousands of former informants in a long-delayed reckoning with the country's repressive past. The move was spearheaded by Prime Minister Peter Magyar, who ousted Viktor Orban in April on a promise of regime change and pressed ahead with a bill granting unrestricted public access to the records for the first time.
items.title: Hungary Releases Communist-Era Informer Files Under Magyar Government

items.summary: Australian frozen yoghurt chain Yo-Chi is opening its newest outlet at i12 Katong on Thursday (Nov 5) at 11am. The launch features a collaboration with heritage bakery Chin Mee Chin, offering two limited-edition toppings—the Kaya Swiss Roll and the kaya-filled Choux Puff—for three days only. A new Iced Latte yoghurt flavour is also introduced.
items.title: Yo-Chi Opens Katong Outlet With Chin Mee Chin Toppings and New Iced Latte Yoghurt

items.summary: According to StockEdge's technical scan data, eight stocks in the Nifty200 pack had closing prices that crossed above their 200-day moving averages on November 4, 2026. Traders use the 200-day DMA as a key indicator of overall trend; when a stock stays above it on the daily timeframe, it is generally read as being in an uptrend.
items.title: Eight Nifty200 Stocks Cross Above Their 200-Day Moving Averages

items.summary: ENIL posted consolidated revenue of ₹117 crore for the quarter, including domestic revenue of ₹114 crore. The company said its Ebitda loss in the digital business narrowed to ₹7.5 crore from ₹9.8 crore a year earlier. ENIL remains focused on growing Gaana's subscriber base through partnerships.
items.title: ENIL Reports Q2 Ebitda Rise on Cost Cuts and Lower Digital Losses

items.summary: South Korea's defence ministry announced Thursday it would deploy maritime patrol aircraft and an explosive ordnance disposal team near the Strait of Hormuz to help keep the waterway open. The mission, which will include a destroyer and unmanned vessels, is strictly for non-combat purposes and operates independently of allied forces. Seoul maintains it will not intervene militarily in the US-Iran war that began February 28.
items.title: South Korea Deploys Non-Combat Mission Near Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: DBS announced that board director Anthony Lim will become chairman of DBS Group Holdings and DBS Bank on Jan 1, 2027, succeeding Peter Seah. Mr Seah retires after 16 years at the helm following a period of digital transformation and growth. Mr Lim joined the boards in April 2020 and previously spent 19 years at GIC. CEO Tan Su Shan praised both leaders as distinguished bankers who will guide DBS forward.
items.title: DBS Names Anthony Lim Chairman as Peter Seah Retires

items.summary: The US Treasury Department on Wednesday imposed fresh sanctions on individuals and companies in India and Turkey over alleged support for Iran, Reuters reported. The action is part of the Trump administration's 'Operation Economic Outcast', aimed at restricting Iran's oil-export revenue. It targets an India-based network allegedly providing fraudulent maritime flags to vessels carrying Iranian petroleum, including Suniel Kumar Sharma, his wife Jaspreet Preeti Shahid and nine linked entities. Separately, Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc was designated for supporting Iran's aviation sector. The Treasury said earlier sanctions had contributed to a sharp decline in the rial and domestic inflation approaching 90%. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington would keep targeting those facilitating support for Tehran by land, sea or air. "We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime," he said.
items.title: US Sanctions Indian Entities Over Iran Oil and Aviation Support

items.summary: The remains of Jenny Balcarras and her daughter Selah Reed were found after their family reported them missing on Sunday. Investigators say multiple grizzly bears could have been involved in the attack, which killed both women in British Columbia. They are continuing to search for the bears, which will be killed for public safety.
items.title: Investigators probe deadly grizzly bear attack in British Columbia

items.summary: The Guardian enlisted a team of critics to review the six books on the Booker Prize 2026 shortlist, which pits literary heavyweights against first-time nominees. The judging panel, led by classicist Mary Beard and including poet Raymond Antrobus, musician Jarvis Cocker, editor Rebecca Liu, and novelist Patricia Lockwood, settled its choice after reading 163 books in seven months. The list includes two past winners—Marlon James and Douglas Stuart—as well as debut novels from Luke Kennard and Rebecca Perry, plus genre fiction by M John Harrison. The review covers each title's premise, tone, and themes before noting the £50,000 ($95,000) prize will be awarded in London on November 9 (November 10 in Australia).
items.title: Critics review six Booker Prize 2026 shortlisted novels

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued a high alert for heavy rains across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh on November 5 as Cyclone Murasu dissipated. For Delhi-NCR it forecast shallow morning fog with maximum temperatures around 27°C to 29°C and minimums of 15°C to 17°C, both below normal. The Central Pollution Control Board reported the AQI at 368 in 'very poor' conditions on Thursday morning, with Punjabi Bagh reaching 458 in the 'severe' category.
items.title: IMD Warns of Heavy Rains in South; Delhi Air Quality Stays Poor

items.summary: Finshots explains why India has not expanded its emergency oil reserves despite importing nearly 90% of crude and facing calls from former RBI governor C. Rangarajan to stockpile more. The country's ISPRL-managed strategic reserve holds about 5.33 million tonnes, roughly a week of imports at current inventory levels. Expansion (Phase II) is stalled by cost—building facilities could run ₹15,000 crore and filling them over ₹25,000 crore to ₹40,000 crore—and delays in construction. Suggested fixes include buying crude when prices are low, a revolving fund, and joint stockpiling with producers like ADNOC.
items.title: Why India Has Not Built Bigger Emergency Oil Reserves

items.summary: Tiger mosquitoes, once confined to tropical regions, are now established across several European countries and moving north roughly 60 kilometres a year. Health authorities warn the diseases they carry — dengue, chikungunya and Zika — could follow. By end of October 2026, Italy reported 76 locally acquired dengue cases and France eight, about twice the previous year's totals. Portugal released 30,000 sterile male mosquitoes in a second attempt to curb populations. Experts stress that elimination is unrealistic; instead they emphasize surveillance, community engagement and preparing diagnostics — with HERA funding €10 million for new tools.
items.title: Europe Races to Contain Spreading Tiger Mosquitoes and Tropical Diseases

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi attacked Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann over his anti-drug record, alleging he smelled of alcohol during a parliamentary sitting around 11 am. Speaking at the Congress Insaaf Rally in Sangrur on November 4, Gandhi questioned whether Mann could fight drug abuse while consuming it regularly and challenged the AAP's promise to eradicate drugs from Punjab. The remarks intensified the Congress-AAP contest ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections despite both parties being INDIA bloc allies nationally. The Aam Aadmi Party responded by calling the rally 'directionless' and accusing Congress of electoral decline.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi's alcohol remark at Bhagwant Mann sparks AAP rebuttal ahead of Punjab polls

items.summary: The Delhi Police transferred Inspector Arun Kumar on Wednesday, a day after suspending Assistant Commissioner of Police Manasvi Vashisht following a protest by over 100 police personnel outside the headquarters. The officers demanded reinstatement and to present their version of an October 23 incident at Shahdara station that left advocate Lalit Bansal injured. Kumar was moved again to the Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations Branch, per an order from the Delhi Police Commissioner's office.
items.title: Delhi Police Inspector Transferred Again After ACP Suspension

items.summary: Kerala Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan said former governor Rajendra Arlekar did not consult the state government before recommending to President Droupadi Murmu the removal of Public Service Commission chairman MR Baiju after irregularities in recruitment exams surfaced. This was the first such recommendation by a Kerala governor, and the Crime Branch is probing the matter.
items.title: Satheesan says ex-governor bypassed state on PSC chief removal

items.summary: Democrats won sweeping majorities in both chambers of Congress after the US midterm elections, setting up a confrontation with President Donald Trump over his legislative agenda. Though they gained room to advance bills, Democrats remain short of the two-thirds majority needed to override vetoes. Trump has signalled he may use veto power and the unoverridable pocket veto to block legislation, while also threatening bills before passage via Statements of Administration Policy.
items.title: Trump's Veto Powers After Democratic Midterm Gains

items.summary: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), through its National Cybercrime Threat Analysis Unit in coordination with CERT-In, issued an advisory on November 3, 2026 warning banks, NBFCs and fintech firms of a rising threat from AI-assisted cyberattacks targeting payment APIs. The advisory explains that criminals exploit unpatched software, misconfigured servers and agentic AI to move multi-crore funds at machine speed through mule accounts before deleting records. It urges stronger API security, transaction monitoring and beneficiary verification, and reiterates the six-hour incident-reporting rule to CERT-In and RBI's DAKSH portal.
items.title: I4C Alerts Financial Firms to AI-Powered Payment API Attacks

items.summary: The US State Department designated two individuals and one entity accused of helping Iran obtain man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS). The targets are Mohammed Ali Tolibov, CEO of Belarus-based Armory Alliance; Nigeria-based Vanguard Tactical Supply Limited; and Russia-based Alisher Domullodzhanov. Officials allege the network sought to procure Chinese-origin MANPADS for Iran using false end-users.
items.title: US Sanctions Three Over Alleged Iran MANPADS Supply Efforts

items.summary: Brent crude and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell below the $100-per-barrel threshold on Thursday, reaching their lowest levels in over two months amid reactions to the US midterm elections. Brent slipped below $95 while WTI dropped under $90 as markets weighed expectations that a Democratic congressional majority could pressure President Donald Trump toward a negotiated settlement with Iran. Oil inventories also fell 865,000 barrels last week.
items.title: Crude oil prices fall below $100 after US midterm elections

items.summary: Electrek reviews BLUETTI's new Apex 200 portable power station, launching November 4 with standalone early-bird pricing starting at $1,099 through November 18. The unit offers 2.56kWh of storage and 3.2kW continuous AC output, expandable to 33.28kWh via up to six B500K batteries. It features built-in RV connections, a tilted display, four app-controllable outlets, and Alexa compatibility. BLUETTI positions it as an easier-to-handle alternative to the Apex 300 for buyers wanting portability with room to scale capacity over time.
items.title: BLUETTI Launches Compact Apex 200 Power Station for Homes and RVs

items.summary: After Democrats routed Republicans Tuesday, analysts say a new era of energy and climate politics begins — one shaped by voters' demand for cheap power rather than decarbonization ambition. New members embraced an 'all of the above' approach, restoring wind and solar tax credits while accepting fossil fuels as status quo. The wave reflects both Trump's failed fossil-fuel agenda and Democrats learning from his mistakes on affordability.
items.title: Democrats’ Energy Moderation Follows Trump’s Climate Reversal

items.summary: Punishing gas prices and a new car affordability crisis are pushing used-car buyers toward electric vehicles, so these used EVs are selling fast across dealer lots. iSeeCars reports the Toyota BZ4x, Lexus RZ300e, Honda Prologue and Polestar 2 average 35 days or less on inventory, with the Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron Quattro at just 29.8 days. Meanwhile, used EVs averaged $32,533 in September 2026, up $2,896 from a year earlier.
items.title: High Gas Prices Drive Unprecedented Used EV Demand

items.summary: About 10 State Disaster Response Force personnel were feared missing after their boats were suspected to have capsized while rescuing fishermen stranded in Bethupalli lake in Khammam district of Telangana on Wednesday evening, official sources said. The operation took place amid heavy rains under cyclone 'Murasu'. Officials and NDRF teams rushed to rescue the personnel.
items.title: Ten SDRF Personnel Feared Missing After Boats Capsize in Telangana

items.summary: After Democrats took control of Congress in the November midterm, analysts say anger over data centers has become a political force that may limit where and how they are built. Exit polls showed more than half of respondents believe AI will do more harm than good, while almost 80% oppose building them nearby; nearly 60% called them a major voting factor. States like Ohio passed bans or face delays in Georgia and Texas, and candidates across several states won by opposing the buildout. Nadine Smith of Color of Change framed Tuesday's election as a referendum on who this economy is built for.
items.title: Midterm backlash against data centers could reshape AI buildout

items.summary: Transport Minister A. Vijay Thamizhan Parthiban announced that TNSTC would run a total of 15,659 buses including 9.086 special buses from November 5 to 7 to meet the passenger demand during the Deepavali celebrations. Services in the return direction numbered 11,967 including 6,815 special buses on November 9 and 10.
items.title: Tamil Nadu minister announces extra buses for Deepavali travel rush

items.summary: A report frames Sub-Saharan Africa as a growing natural gas and liquefied natural gas frontier, with buyers shifting away from the Strait of Hormuz. Fitch forecasts SSA’s LNG exports will rise nearly 175% to 98 billion cubic meters by 2034, up from 35.7 bcm in 2024. The African Energy Chamber projects ~$40 billion a year flowing into upstream investment through 2030, lifting hydrocarbon output to 12.5 MMboe/d. Projects are highlighted across Mozambique’s Rovuma Basin, Nigeria’s Train 7 expansion and the Greater Tortue Ahmeyim project in Senegal and Mauritania.
items.title: Africa LNG Exports Projected to Jump as Buyers Avoid Hormuz

items.summary: The piece reflects on Diwali, noting that while homes are cleaned and streets lit each year, many hearts remain restless despite the display of light. It frames the festival's tradition around inner illumination rather than material celebration, citing examples like Shri Ram's return to Ayodhya and Mahavira's enlightenment as symbols of spiritual renewal. The author urges readers to pause before lighting decorative lamps and instead reflect on awakening their own awareness.
items.title: Diwali as a Call for Inner Spiritual Renewal

items.summary: The Supreme Court directed the Madhya Pradesh Assembly Speaker to decide within two months a disqualification plea against rebel Congress MLA Nirmala Sapre under the anti-defection law, which had been pending for over two years. The petition was filed in July 2024 by Leader of Opposition Umang Singhar, who alleges that Sapre abandoned her Congress membership and joined the BJP after winning on a Congress ticket in 2023. Sapre has denied resigning from Congress or joining the BJP.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Speaker To Rule On Disqualification Plea Within Two Months

items.summary: Oracle has cancelled a $7 billion chip leasing deal with Tencent, according to the Financial Times. The newspaper reported in October that Oracle had signed a five-year agreement to lease 100,000 chips to Tencent. US officials reportedly raised concerns about the arrangement, citing two sources familiar with the matter.
items.title: Oracle Cancels Billion-Dollar Chip Deal With Tencent After US Pushback

items.summary: Catalist-listed iX Biopharma replied to Singapore Exchange queries on Nov 3, 2026, clarifying that its prospective US manufacturing partner Orion Specialty Labs has not yet obtained a Nevada state licence and that the joint venture agreement remains unsigned. The exchange questioned this after an Oct 20 report found Orion’s application had been postponed twice, contradicting iX Biopharma’s Nov 2025 claim of “operationally ready infrastructure and regulatory licences.” iX Biopharma said it meant Orion’s FDA 503B registration and that the state licence would follow finalisation. Its US$41 million Pentagon ketamine wafer deal, awarded in February, was described as separate from the joint venture.
items.title: iX Biopharma Defends US Manufacturing Licence After SGX Query

items.summary: Per Financial Times, Microsoft rejected an option to more than double its agreement with Nscale for renting computing power at a Texas data center, walking away from a deal worth tens of billions of dollars. Reuters could not verify the report.
items.title: Microsoft rejects multibillion-dollar AI deal with UK's Nscale, FT reports

items.summary: On November 5, 2026, OpenAI announced it would acquire Pierre Computer Company, the developer of open-source coding tools including Trees, Diffs and Code Storage. The deal aims to expand its Codex platform's capabilities in building, understanding and reviewing software as AI agents take on more development tasks. Pierre's projects will remain open-source, though closing depends on regulatory approvals.
items.title: OpenAI Acquires Pierre Computer Company to Expand Codex Coding Tools

items.summary: According to a Bloomberg report, Apple is reducing employee access to AI tools as part of broader cost-cutting efforts despite encouraging wider adoption. The iPhone maker reportedly cut daily AI usage budgets for some engineers from $300 to $200 last month and may lower engineering teams' allowances further to $100. Non-engineering teams could face tighter limits, with some employees already capped at $100 or potentially as low as $25 per day. Bloomberg noted these changes reflect Apple balancing cost control against AI adoption goals.
items.title: Apple Trims Employee AI Spending Amid Cost-Cutting Push

items.summary: Reuters reports that Google's parent Alphabet has expanded voluntary exit programmes with severance packages in five countries, including the US and Switzerland, as it invests heavily in AI infrastructure. In Switzerland, participants received one month's salary per year of service, capped at 12 months' salary. Exact terms for Canada, France, Germany and Japan remain undisclosed. The programme excludes some roles and divisions such as DeepMind. Google has not disclosed total eligibility or headcount reduction targets. Microsoft separately announced a similar buyout covering around 60,000 employees in October 2026. A Google spokesperson confirmed the expansion to Reuters.
items.title: Google Expands Voluntary Exit Packages Amid AI Spending Push

items.summary: Regional Indian airlines are urging the Civil Aviation Ministry to revive the withdrawn Price Stabilization Fund with flexible terms as aviation turbine fuel prices hit an all-time high of 137 rupees per litre. Fuel expenses have risen from 40 per cent to nearly 60 per cent of total operating costs, straining carriers that provide last-mile connectivity and prompting them to seek special provisions under the government formula.
items.title: Indian Airlines Urge Revival of Fuel Price Stabilization Fund Amid Jet Fuel Cost Surge

items.summary: Google co-founder Larry Page once said he would consider leaving his entire fortune to Elon Musk rather than a traditional charity. The remark surfaced during a 2014 TED interview with Charlie Rose, who quoted an earlier statement in which Page expressed confidence that Musk could change the future. Their friendship reportedly cooled over disagreements about AI risks.
items.title: Larry Page Said He Would Leave His Fortune to Elon Musk

items.summary: A Bloomberg report and Reserve Bank data show India's household debt jumped 36% over a year, with consumer credit hitting a record 46% of GDP. Rising rates may strain borrowers; Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman expects consumption to stay strong while experts worry about falling savings.
items.title: Rising EMIs Trap Indian Buyers in Debt Web

items.summary: MIT researchers have created a new memory system called UQ-DAAAM (Uncertainty Quantification for Describe Anything, Anywhere, at Any Moment) designed to help robots correct mislabeled objects in their stored memories. The system compares multiple descriptions of the same object from different viewpoints to quantify uncertainty and refine inaccurate captions. Principal investigator Luca Carlone explained that allowing robots to recognize what they do not know is essential for safe deployment. Testing showed the refinement step resolved about 92 percent of ambiguous objects while requiring only two additional captions per object, improving description accuracy by 5 percent compared to prior methods.
items.title: MIT Researchers Develop Robot Memory System

items.summary: Google is extending voluntary exit offers with severance packages to select employees in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland as it cuts costs while increasing AI investment. DeepMind and Google Cloud are excluded because they need more staff. The company has not disclosed how many accepted the offer. Microsoft's similar buyout scheme follows amid rising tech spending on artificial intelligence.
items.title: Google Extends Voluntary Exit Offers Amid AI Investment Push

items.summary: Google Research has released Agile Deliberation, a human-in-the-loop framework that helps users define boundaries for subjective image concepts such as healthy food or clickbait. Rather than assuming users know the concept limits, it prompts Gemini models without fine-tuning and finds borderline images by meaning instead of classifier confidence. The design drew on interviews with content moderation experts who scoped concepts before refining them on ambiguous examples. Evaluation ran 18 live sessions totaling about 90 minutes each, with nine participants labeling 200 held-out test images per concept across paid-to-play clickbait and healthy food. On average, F1 rose 10.5 points above zero-shot Gemini 2.5 Flash.
items.title: Google Research Releases Framework for Classifying Subjective Images

items.summary: Apple lowered daily AI spending caps for some engineers from $300 to $200 last month, with deeper cuts planned as low as $100 a day. Bloomberg reported the changes via anonymous sources amid anxiety about layoffs under new CEO John Ternus, who took office on September 1 and is pushing cost discipline. Reactions are divided: some staff say few used full allowances; others see wider job losses ahead.
items.title: Apple Tightens Employee AI Spending Amid Layoff Fears

items.summary: Washington: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company, the developer of open-source coding tools, to expand its Codex platform's capabilities in building, understanding and reviewing software. The acquisition brings Pierre's team and technology into OpenAI's developer ecosystem, including tools such as Trees, Diffs and Highlights. Following the deal, Pierre's projects remain open-source.
items.title: OpenAI Acquires Pierre Computer Company To Expand Codex AI Coding Tools & Strengthen AI-Powered Software Development

items.summary: U.S. solar power purchase agreement prices rose 4.9% quarter over quarter in the third quarter of 2026, returning to an upward trend after a second-quarter decline, per LevelTen Energy's report. Wind PPA prices stayed flat despite jumping nearly 14% over the past year. The authors suggest buyers act soon amid policy misalignment and upcoming tariff effects on polysilicon.
items.title: Solar PPA Prices Rise in Q3 Amid Section 232 Tariffs

items.summary: China's trade in services rose 8.5% year on year in the first nine months of 2026, reaching 5.77 trillion yuan (about $858.89 billion), according to the Ministry of Commerce. Exports climbed 14.8% while imports grew 4.8%, leaving a deficit of 1.23 trillion yuan. Transport services led with a 33.9% jump, and knowledge-intensive services expanded 7.4%. Beijing is promoting new trade drivers through its Five-Year Plan and demonstration zones in 16 cities.
items.title: China's Services Trade Grows as Beijing Pushes New Drivers

items.summary: Following Democrats' congressional majority, trade and legal experts say they have gained oversight authority over agency funding and committee hearings on President Donald Trump's tariffs, but remain largely unable to override his veto of tariff repeals or rescind trade authorities. Blake Harden of Ernst & Young said the election is unlikely to significantly impact the president's agenda because much trade power remains in the executive branch. Democrats would need 67 senators to overcome a filibuster and 290 House members to override a veto, making near-term policy changes uncertain while Trump pursues new tariffs under Section 301 investigations.
items.title: Democrats Gain Trade Oversight but Face Trump Veto Wall

items.summary: The writer, who says Ningbo is their hometown, describes returning there with the goal of showing places beyond well-known landmarks. They mention a morning market, an old library, and a lively waterfront as examples of what lies past typical tourist sights. Framing cities as having stories that extend past postcard images, they invite readers to look past guidebooks at parts of Ningbo rarely seen.
items.title: A traveler returns home to explore lesser-known Ningbo

items.summary: Ather Energy shares fell about 4%, ending a five-day gain, amid an upcoming lock-up expiry. Nuvama Alternative & Quantitative Research says roughly 77 million Ather Energy shares will become eligible for trading after the expiry, around 21% of total outstanding equity, though promoters may retain most. The EV scooter-maker reported its first quarterly net profit of Rs 1.26 crore in the September quarter of FY27, a turnaround from a Rs 154 crore loss a year earlier, with revenue up nearly 63% YoY to Rs 1,464 crore and EBITDA turning positive at Rs 11.3 crore.
items.title: Ather Energy Shares Fall as Lock-up Expiry Looms

items.summary: India's government is reviewing customs duty concessions covering 118 products while relaxing GST rules on post-sale discounts. The changes aim to rationalise indirect taxation, encourage domestic manufacturing and reduce compliance hurdles for manufacturers, importers and consumer-facing businesses. A review by BDO India's Karthik Iyer called the exercise timely but cautioned that exemptions should be withdrawn gradually where imported inputs remain essential, while Mani noted documentation of credit notes must continue even as invoice-linkage conditions ease. The two moves are framed as part of a broader effort to correct inverted duty structures and align tax policy with commercial realities.
items.title: Centre reviews customs duty relief for 118 products, eases GST on post-sale discounts

items.summary: Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne says Canada must urgently diversify its trade, branding Thursday's budget 'Masters of our Destiny.' He plans support for workers in autos and steel hurt by tariffs. Dominic LeBlanc noted tariff talks will go with the White House, not Congress. Optimism about a deal follows midterm losses that could end Trump's protectionist measures.
items.title: Canada Budget Aims to Diversify Trade Amid Trump Tariffs

items.summary: Nearly 90 foreign military attachés from more than 50 countries visited Zunyi, Guizhou Province, China. On Tuesday the delegation laid a flower basket at the Zunyi Red Army Martyrs Cemetery to honor fallen heroes. The visit came at the invitation of China's Ministry of National Defense and forms part of a six-day program across Guizhou and Sichuan provinces, during which the group toured revolutionary sites and institutions.
items.title: Foreign Military Attachés Honor Long March Martyrs in Zunyi

items.summary: Adora Flora City, China's second domestically built large cruise ship, will be delivered in Shanghai on November 6 after four years of construction. The vessel has 2,130 cabins and can hold up to 5,232 passengers at full capacity. Commercial voyages are scheduled to begin on November 22, focusing on southern China and the Southeast Asian market.
items.title: China's Second Domestically Built Large Cruise Ship Nears Delivery

items.summary: Ashutosh Ranka, leader of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), challenged Union minister Jitendra Singh after the latter alleged that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke received financial support from Pakistani politicians and handlers. The claims were made during a press conference in Bengaluru on November 3. Singh said Dipke was funded by US-based donors, while Ranka allegedly took money through intermediaries. Ranka responded with questions about the minister's negotiations, and Dipke shared a video of the comments alongside a satirical GIF.
items.title: CJP Leader Rebuts Minister's Pakistan Funding Allegations

items.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that the constitutional requirement to produce an accused before a magistrate within 24 hours begins at detention, not formal arrest, treating both as curtailing liberty equally. The court rejected artificial distinctions between the two and criticised several high courts for drawing them. It also held that fundamental rights must take precedence over special laws such as UAPA, NDPS Act and PMLA in bail and trial-delay cases.
