items.title: Supreme Court Ties Arrest Clock to Detention Time

items.summary: CleanTechnica argues Elon Musk spent at least $474 million on the 2026 midterm elections, though his endorsed candidates were defeated decisively. The article notes this was reportedly his largest losing political effort since 1974 and that voters in targeted jurisdictions rejected him as a poor choice. It observes Musk concentrated spending in Texas despite an unexpected Democratic blue wave there, while noting Democrats champion the clean energy and electric vehicle policies central to Musk's business interests. Talarico stated 'Texas is not for sale,' after losing to Musk-backed opposition with at least $150 million spent against him. The piece speculates whether these electoral losses could ultimately benefit Tesla under new Democratic leadership rather than concluding it definitively.
items.title: Musk's $474 Million Midterm Spending Wasted Amid Texas Blue Wave

items.summary: Joshua Wong, a leading figure in Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement, was sentenced on Thursday to 10 years in jail for colluding with foreign forces under the city's national security law. He had already served six years and pleaded guilty earlier this year; two months of his new term will run concurrently. Prosecutors said he conspired with self-exiled activist Nathan Law between July and late November 2020 to lobby for sanctions against Beijing. Hong Kong's chief executive John Lee called the pair primary culprits in undermining stability, while Human Rights Watch condemned the ruling as cruel and unjust. Wong has been imprisoned multiple times since his activism began as a teenager.
items.title: Hong Kong Activist Joshua Wong Sentenced Under National Security Law

items.summary: In the 2026 US midterms, Democrat Scott Colom leads incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by just 1,138 votes with almost 96% of Mississippi's ballots counted. Democrats have not won a Mississippi Senate seat since 1982. As Republicans begin assigning blame for their losses, coverage continues across the country.
items.title: Democrats eye historic upset in Mississippi Senate race amid Republican blame game

items.summary: After Democrats won a larger-than-expected US election, the article asks whether they can turn an affordability promise into policy. Voters reportedly focused on grocery, electricity and fuel bills rather than statistics, with just 21% of Americans satisfied with the country's direction. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said winning was only the start; now it is time to govern on affordability. But President Trump retains veto power, requiring a two-thirds majority to override. Economist Bernard Yaros expects average import tariffs near 10% for most of Trump's term and sees no subsidy deal until late 2027, with benefits in 2028. Oxford Economics warns further escalation appears more likely now that petrol prices matter less politically. Government funding also runs out after 11 December, raising shutdown risk. The piece notes Democrats won governorships in Texas, Ohio and Georgia but face limits on what Congress can pass before the next election.
items.title: Democratic affordability win faces veto and delivery hurdles

items.summary: Historic England added nearly 200 sites, including Hastings Castle, Charles Dickens’ Rochester chalet and wildfire-blasted Fylingdales Moor, to its heritage at risk register. Joint chief executive Emma Squire said even very special places can face decay or loss, pointing to climate emergency, hotter summers and coastal erosion as drivers. Around 85 sites were removed after restoration; the organisation spent more than £12m on repairs in 2025-26 while almost 5,000 remain listed.
items.title: Historic England Adds Norman Castle and Dickens Chalet to At-Risk Register

items.summary: Frances Ryan, a Guardian columnist, argues that the Home Office's plan to exempt an estimated 280,000 care workers from waiting periods for settlement is inconsistent with Labour's broader immigration rules. The home secretary announced this week that these workers could apply for indefinite leave to remain after five years, but eligibility is limited to those earning £25,000 a year who entered the scheme before 2025. Ryan contends the policy rewards wealth while dismissing working-class labour and questions its logic amid social care staff shortages.
items.title: Guardian columnist questions Labour's care worker visa policy

items.summary: A BBC London piece asks why identical goods cost different amounts across the capital, using Greggs sausage rolls (£1.35 in Sutton versus £1.60 central), Pizza Express pizzas (from £20.95 to £22.95) and Pets At Home rabbit castrations (£70 in Enfield up to £136 in Chingford). Consumer expert Helen Dewdney of the Complaining Cow says convenience, transport links like Tube access and local costs drive the gaps; petrol prices also differ pump to pump (unleaded 171.9p–177.9p per litre on one day). Greggs uses national pricing but allows variation where costs are higher. Pets At Home said its Vets for Pets practices set fees locally, citing operating cost rises and local needs. The article urges shoppers to compare prices rather than assume parity across branches.
items.title: London Chain Prices Vary by Location, Experts Say

items.summary: Prominent Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong was sentenced Thursday to a ten-year prison term for his second conviction under Beijing-imposed national security law, in what critics say reflects the crackdown on the city's pro-democracy movement. He pleaded guilty last September to conspiracy charges and had been expected to be freed by January 2027 after serving four years eight months of another sentence; a judge said he could serve both terms concurrently. Judge William Tam called the offense grave, starting from a thirteen-year baseline before reducing it for the plea. Supporters say the ruling further chills civic activism as authorities keep prominent figures imprisoned.
items.title: Hong Kong Activist Joshua Wong Sentenced to Ten Years

items.summary: A new study examines how artificial light at night affects wildlife across 21 protected areas in Kerala's Western Ghats, using satellite data from 2024. Researchers found that within reserves, places of worship most strongly predicted light levels, while surrounding roads and activity centres mattered more outside boundaries. Light exposure increased with distance, suggesting pollution comes from the wider landscape too.
items.title: Study Examines Artificial Light Effects in Kerala's Protected Areas

items.summary: Sony reported a 45 per cent rise in second-quarter operating profit of 622.3 billion yen ($3.95 billion), beating market estimates, driven by stronger results at its games and movies units. The performance prompted Sony to raise its full-year profit outlook by 9 per cent, with the film Spider-Man: Brand New Day cited as a contributor.
items.title: Sony Posts Sharp Q2 Profit Rise

items.summary: The International Court of Justice will deliver a landmark ruling on Nov. 19 on whether Myanmar's crackdown against the mostly Muslim Rohingya minority constituted genocide, officials said Tuesday. Judges have for seven years weighed accusations by The Gambia that the repression breached the 1948 U.N. Genocide Convention. While the court cannot enforce its decisions, a finding of genocide would increase international pressure on leader Min Aung Hlaing.
items.title: Top U.N. Court Set to Rule on Myanmar Rohingya Genocide Case

items.summary: A parliamentary business select committee found that Britain is dangerously dependent on China for critical minerals needed for defence, renewable energy and AI. The committee called for a centralised policy and finance facility to diversify supply, noting bottlenecks in refining seven mineral categories and forecast lithium demand rising 45-fold by 2030. Committee chair Liam Byrne said the UK cannot rearm or deliver net zero without securing these minerals. A government spokesperson denied lacking a strategy, citing £400m for domestic production and recycling toward 10% of demand domestically and 20% through recycling by 2035, with no more than 60% from any single country.
items.title: UK MPs Warn of Critical Minerals Reliance on China

items.summary: The National Police Agency announced Thursday it will begin sharing information on bank accounts used in scams with financial institutions nationwide, aiming to identify fraud victims early and prevent further losses amid rising special-fraud losses of ¥261 billion from January to September.
items.title: Japan police to share scam account data with banks

items.summary: In an episode of his podcast, Robert J. Shiller—referred to here only as COWEN—and Richard Hanania (HANANIA) discuss Joseph Conrad's novel The Secret Agent, though the transcript references Nostromo repeatedly. Their conversation covers the book's political backdrop, its scrambled timeline, and the near-absence of religion in Conrad's world. Cowen argues that the novel critiques classical liberalism as a form of corruption, while Hanania pushes back on readings centered on GDP versus moral progress. They debate whether characters like Sotillo represent primitive cruelty or noble savagery, ultimately agreeing that politics is an unromantic realm and that Conrad occupies a moderate position between socialism and classical liberalism on their one-to-ten scale.
items.title: Cowen and Hanania Discuss Conrad's Nostromo

items.summary: After losing US midterm elections partly over high gasoline prices, President Donald Trump acknowledged fuel costs as a political liability while arguing they were a short-term effect of the war in Iran. Analyst Patrick De Haan of GasBuddy said crude price declines could push the national average below $4 per gallon within days; it stood at $4.12 on Wednesday morning. Brent crude fell 8.3% to under $100, and WTI dropped to around $88.12. Democratic control of Congress may pressure Trump's war posture, though renewed escalation could reverse the trend. Tom Kloza of Gulf Oil expects seasonal conditions to favour lower prices over the next six weeks if tensions ease.
items.title: Trump's Midterm Setback and Falling Oil Prices

items.summary: Ben Yole, a prominent Tasmanian harness racing trainer, has had his company placed into liquidation after owing more than $735,000. A report lodged with ASIC states the company held no real estate or equipment but did own motor vehicles. Separately, Mr Yole was disqualified from the racing industry following animal welfare issues.
items.title: Harness Racing Trainer's Company Enters Liquidation

items.summary: Ghanakanta Gogoi, a Guwahati businessperson accused of killing five people near a hotel on October 26 over a lease dispute, was shot dead by police during an alleged gunfight Wednesday while trying to escape custody. He had been sent to judicial custody Tuesday and ordered not to leave jail after sunset. Police said he attempted to seize a service weapon as the team traveled about 350 km from Guwahati to Sibsagar.
items.title: Guwahati hotel shooting suspect killed in police gunfight

items.summary: Former soldier Nathan Heckel told the Supreme Court that Masood Zakaria, an accused murderer fighting to have two gangland murder charges dismissed after his 2023 return from Türkiye, was released from restraints mid-flight. The AFP-paid operation cost $1 million and may affect other prosecutions.
items.title: Security contractor denies zip-tying alleged Sydney crime boss during extradition flight

items.summary:
Vice-President JD Vance blamed his party's midterm defeat on the war in Iran, saying "the reason we lost is the war" and that losing the Senate was not worth it. In a 600-word statement on X, he avoided naming Trump directly while attributing analysis to unnamed pollsters - seen as an effort to distance himself ahead of a possible 2028 presidential run. Trump agreed the midterms were "largely" decided by the war but said he would "do it again." Analysts at CSIS and via BBC interviews read Vance's move as a delicate balancing act, while The New York Times reported he showed the message to Trump before posting it. A possible campaign remains undecided two years away.

The item notes Vance offered a four-point strategy: end the war, focus on cost of living/inflation, put America First, and change relations with Israel.
items.title: Vance Blames Iran War for Midterm Loss, Signals Possible 2028 Run

items.summary: A Hong Kong court sentenced democracy activist Joshua Wong to ten additional years in jail on Thursday for colluding with foreign powers, pushing his release date to late 2036. Judge William Tam set a starting point of 13 years before the guilty plea reduced it; Wong had previously been jailed under the national security law and could have faced life imprisonment. Human Rights Watch called the sentence cruel and unjust, while Beijing welcomed it as proof that foreign pressure is futile.
items.title: Hong Kong Court Sentences Joshua Wong to Ten More Years

items.summary: A new report from consultancy The Brattle Group, published Thursday on behalf of The Pew Charitable Trusts, proposes scaling virtual power plants to blunt the risks of uncertain data center demand. As of 2025, the U.S. had 113 gigawatts of distributed energy resources usable for VPPs; if capacity more than quadrupled to 524 GW by midcentury, it could avoid $614 billion in grid investments and cut average household bills by $122 a year by 2050. In a hypothetical scenario where load growth falls 5% short of forecasts between now and 2030, VPPs would reduce overbuilding costs borne by utility customers from $84 billion to roughly $33 billion through 2040. Lead author Ryan Hledik noted the inherent flexibility of modular resources compared with traditional investments, while Maureen Quinlan of The Pew Charitable Trusts urged utilities and regulators to incorporate these benefits into grid planning.
items.title: Brattle Report Frames Virtual Power Plants as Grid Hedge Against Data Center Uncertainty

items.summary: A three-storey building under construction collapsed Thursday in Chawri Bazar, a crowded area of Old Delhi, according to PTI. Several people are feared trapped beneath the debris. At least six fire department vehicles were at the site overseeing rescue operations, per the news agency. This follows two earlier Delhi collapses: one on September 6 that killed seven and another on October 7 in Seemapuri that killed five.
items.title: Building Collapse Traps Several in Old Delhi Market Area

items.summary: The World Photography Organisation announced that Ghanaian photographer James Barnor will receive the Outstanding Contribution to Photography award at the 2027 Sony World Photography Awards. Now aged 97, Barnor documented Black culture and everyday life across Ghana's independence movement and London's African diaspora for Drum magazine. He is regarded as a pioneer of African photography, with work held by major institutions worldwide.
items.title: Ghana's James Barnor Awarded Top Photography Honour at Age 97

items.summary: BSE shares rose about 4% on second-quarter results showing revenue up 34.1% year-on-year to Rs 1,432.6 crore and EBITDA margin expanding to 68.7%. Motilal Oswal kept a Buy rating with a target of Rs 4,200, citing derivatives recovery after the CAS withdrawal in December 2026. Nuvama holds the stock at Rs 3,810 but stays cautious on valuations.
items.title: BSE shares jump after strong Q2 results; brokers weigh in

items.summary: The Karnataka government announced a price hike across key Nandini dairy products ahead of the Diwali season. A one-litre sachet of ghee rose from 715 rupees to 850 rupees, salted butter reached 380 rupees for 500 grams up from 339 rupees, and paneer climbed from 411 rupees to 485 rupees per kilogram. The increase follows an eight-rupee rise in milk prices aimed at supporting dairy farmers during drought conditions.
items.title: Karnataka Raises Nandini Ghee and Butter Prices Before Diwali

items.summary: Brent crude fell below $94 a barrel on Thursday, its lowest in months, as markets weighed an end to the Middle East war after Donald Trump's Republican Party lost the US midterm elections. Brent traded at $93.50 following an 8.7% prior-session slide; WTI dropped 4.5% to $91.73 and dipped below $87 Thursday. With Democrats now controlling both chambers, markets expect harder war funding and a diplomatic push toward Iran. Reuters quoted Dennis Kissler of BOK Financial saying larger Middle East exports and Trump's no-strike statement are pressuring prices. India may gain as lower costs ease its imports; it imported 59.7 million tonnes in April-June while spending $49 billion, up 26% from $39 billion a year earlier.
items.title: Trump's Midterm Loss and Falling Crude Oil Prices

items.summary: On Thursday, Yemen reported airstrikes and clashes with Houthi rebels across several fronts, according to media reports. Al-Jumhuriya TV said an airstrike destroyed a Houthi missile launcher on Mount Ba'dan in Ibb province, the second such strike there in under 24 hours. Aden TV reported intense fighting on the Lahj front and airstrikes targeting reinforcements elsewhere. Yemeni forces conducted 322 operations since Oct. 5, killing 64 fighters and destroying or disabling 16 vehicles. The clashes resumed after a calm that had held since April 2022, worsening Yemen's humanitarian crisis and displacing more than 250,000 people per UN reports.
items.title: Yemeni Forces Report Airstrikes and Clashes Against Houthis Across Multiple Fronts

items.summary: On Wednesday, Iranians held anti-U.S. and anti-Israel rallies across the country to mark the National Day of Fighting Global Arrogance and denounce what they call U.S.-Israeli hegemony. In Tehran, large crowds gathered outside the former U.S. Embassy compound chanting slogans. Tehran Mayor Alireza Zakani said Iran's struggle with the United States aimed at resisting U.S. oppression. Residents Benyamin and Reza added that Iran must drive the U.S. out of the Middle East.
items.title: Iranians Hold Anti-U.S. and Anti-Israel Rallies Nationwide

items.summary: A three-storey under-construction building collapsed in Chawri Bazar, Old Delhi on Thursday morning around 9:50am, killing two people and injuring one. Eyewitness Mohd Nayeem told ANI he woke to a crashing sound while asleep; injured labourers said about three or four people were inside. Several others are feared trapped. Rescue teams including the NDRF responded amid heavy footfall before Diwali. HT separately reported that Chandni Chowk's 160-year-old Town Hall, owned by the MCD, also collapsed Wednesday.
items.title: Two killed as Old Delhi market building collapses during festive rush

items.summary: Search operations for 10 missing villagers in Gidipabali village were temporarily suspended after three consecutive landslides struck the site overnight. Kandhamal district collector Vedbhushan, leading the operation, said the halt followed consultations with technical experts and cited treacherous weather plus further-landslide risk. He stressed it was not permanent and would resume when conditions improve. Rescuers recovered two bodies; survivors say remaining ones may lie more than 30 feet deep beyond current equipment reach. The state mobilised over 400 personnel, including NDRF, ODRAF and Fire Services teams. Families have proposed a mass funeral and memorial for the victims to be discussed by district officials.
items.title: Rescue Halted After Landslides Bury Odisha Villagers

items.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on November 5, 2026 that two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz. According to IRNA, one tanker struck a mine while using an unauthorized route south of the strait; another supertanker caught fire leaving the eastern part, and a tugboat attempting to help also burned.
items.title: Iran Says Three Vessels Catch Fire in Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: Profits at roughly two-thirds of BSE 100 companies reporting results rose 20% in the September quarter, per Citigroup Inc., marking fastest growth in five quarters and beating estimates. The gains may revive interest in India’s $5.1 trillion market after foreign outflows soured sentiment. Since Oct. 1, the Nifty 50 gained 6% while MSCI Asia Pacific fell 7.5%. Risks include high oil prices pressuring inflation and the rupee.
items.title: Indian Earnings Rise Bolster Case for India Stocks as Asia Wavers

items.summary: Voters across South Africa cast ballots Wednesday in local government elections marked by anger over water and power failures, with turnout at 12 million of 29.2 million registered voters by 5:00 pm. The vote for 257 councils comes as polls indicate a further decline in support for the ANC, which fell below 50 percent in 2021 and secured just over 40 percent nationally in 2024. Coalition governments are expected where no party wins an outright majority.
items.title: South African Voters Turn Out Amid Power and Water Failures

items.summary: A three-storey under-construction building collapsed on Thursday morning at Gali Sitara near the Chawri Bazaar Metro station in Old Delhi, officials said. At least two people died and several others were feared trapped under the debris. The incident occurred nearly two months after a five-storey building collapse killed seven people in south Delhi.
items.title: Three-Storey Building Collapse Kills Two in Delhi Bazaar

items.summary: A Hong Kong court sentenced democracy activist Joshua Wong to ten more years in prison on Thursday for colluding with foreign powers. He pleaded guilty in September 2025 to seeking sanctions against Hong Kong and China under Beijing's national security law, after already serving nearly six years behind bars. Authorities charged him again in June 2025 over asking other countries to impose penalties. Rights groups called the charge a deliberate attempt to keep him jailed, while analyst Steve Tsang said Beijing intends to make an example of Wong as it keeps tight control over Hong Kong.
items.title: Hong Kong Court Sentences Joshua Wong to Ten More Years Over Foreign Collusion

items.summary: Crude oil prices and energy stocks declined after Democratic candidates won both houses of the U.S. Congress, with markets anticipating policy shifts. Brent crude traded at $94.30 per barrel, down 9% on Wednesday; West Texas Intermediate was at $87.35 per barrel, down 8%. The S&P Energy index fell 4.77% to 976.18 amid expectations of changes in U.S. foreign and energy policy linked to Democratic victories in Texas and Georgia over opposition to new data center construction.
items.title: Oil Prices Fall After Democrats Win U.S. Midterms

items.summary: BK Hariprasad, President of the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee, said on Thursday that the INDIA bloc’s protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls would continue until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns. The demonstration at Freedom Park in Bengaluru is organised by Congress and allied parties, with District Congress presidents holding rallies across Karnataka from tomorrow onward.
items.title: Karnataka Congress Chief Vows INDIA Bloc Protest Until CEC Resigns

items.summary: Delhi's air quality index reached 377 on Wednesday, classified as 'very poor,' with a thick grey haze covering the city. Residents report breathing difficulties and burning eyes. Experts warn it may worsen during Diwali fireworks on November 6-7 due to crackers and farm fires in Punjab. The government has urged power plants to switch to biomass.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Hits Near-400 AQI Ahead of Diwali

items.summary: An international team of lawyers filed a coordinated battery of lawsuits against JBS, the world’s largest meat company, and its financiers on Wednesday. The 14 legal actions in four European jurisdictions accuse JBS and affiliated banks, asset managers, accountants and lawyers of criminal complicity over cattle bought from deforested land. A coalition-commissioned study by AidEnvironment found JBS linked to more than 16 million deforested acres. George Collecott said regulators should investigate whether the institutions failed their due diligence obligations. Barclays reviewed the complaint but declined further comment; other defendants did not respond.
items.title: Lawyers Accuse JBS of Amazon Money Laundering

items.summary: Georgia voters handed Democrats control of the Public Service Commission, breaking a Republican majority that lasted from 2006 to 2025 and giving them their first seat since then. The shift comes amid voter frustration over rising electricity bills tied to data center expansion and nuclear Plant Vogtle rate increases. Commissioners regulate utility rates and oversee Georgia Power. Democrats Peter Hubbard and Sheila Edwards won seats, while Republicans had held a five-zero majority for nearly two decades. Outside spending exceeded $5 million, much supporting the Republican challenger Josh Tolbert through groups like Competence Matters. The new Democratic majority plans to increase scrutiny of Georgia Power and strengthen consumer protections.
items.title: Georgia Voters Give Democrats Control of Energy Regulator for First Time in Three Decades

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Linux Mint 27 is scheduled for release next month as a complete refresh of the desktop distribution. Lead developer Clement “Clem” Lefebvre announced earlier this year that the team was considering slowing its twice-a-year cadence to allow larger changes, prompting an official change in numbering and schedule on Oct. 13th. Mint 27 reintroduces hibernation via a new Sleep Modes page, adds Superlight as a system-monitoring replacement for GNOME System Monitor, gives Nemo file manager a media preview pane, and introduces Velocitty terminal and Unfold archive manager. The release is built on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS with the LMDE installer supporting Secure Boot and LVM/LUKS. Clem noted in the September newsletter he had never seen so many changes for one release; the author expects GIMP 3.2.2 as default editor, replacing Mint 22.3’s older GIMP 2.10.
items.title: Linux Mint 27 Brings Hibernation, New Tools and Ubuntu Base

items.summary: India’s solar photovoltaic sector reached about 172 GW toward its 200 GW target by end of FY 2026–27, with MNRE reporting 171.05 GW installed as of September 2026 and 20.79 GW added in the first half of that year. Industry leaders say growth has been a module-assembly story: domestic cell capacity stays below 40 GW while ingot-wafer output is under one percent, factory utilisation runs around 35–40%, and commercial polysilicon production has not begun. They point to ALMM List-II and upcoming List-III requirements from June 2028 as drivers for upstream investment, alongside storage integration and grid expansion. Companies such as JAKSON, Vikram Solar and Solarworld cite plans ranging from 3 GW of cells to 9 GW of ingot-wafer capacity at Gangaikondan, Tamil Nadu. Many speakers note that crossing 200 GW is a milestone rather than the destination.},
items.title: Solar Firms Warn India Must Build Cells, Not Just Panels

items.summary: Polycab India introduces the PHLVB-5K-AG3, a lithium iron phosphate battery offering 5.12 kWh nominal capacity and 5 kWh usable energy under specified test conditions. The unit supports parallel connection of up to 30 batteries for configurations reaching 150 kWh. It features a dedicated Battery Management System, round-trip efficiency of at least 96%, more than 6,000 cycles at 70% capacity retention, and warranties ranging from eight years with three-phase inverters to ten years with single-phase models. Actual performance depends on temperature, state of charge, and inverter model.
items.title: Polycab Launches Scalable LFP Battery for Solar and Backup Storage

items.summary: In today's session, Ashok Leyland shares rose as much as 12% to Rs 172 on the BSE, while Tata Motors jumped 9% to Rs 440. The rally followed a sharp fall in crude oil prices and buoyant market sentiment after Democrats gained ground in US midterm elections. Analysts expect the bullish trend to continue amid easing global cues, though the article carries investment disclaimers from author Veer Sharma.
items.title: Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland Shares Surge on Crude Oil Drop

items.summary: Google, with the National Police Agency (NPA), said it disabled a backdoor that turned about 1.3 million Videostrong-manufactured Android TV boxes into malware-infected residential proxies. The NPA linked unauthorized bank transfers to these proxies in roughly 1,918 cases worth around ¥2.89 billion ($18.3 million) in 2024.
items.title: Google and Japan's police shut down Chinese backdoor in internet devices

items.summary: Bharti Airtel chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal plans a global satellite network to reduce reliance on the US and China, per Bloomberg. His Eutelsat OneWeb faces SpaceX's Starlink, which has over 10,000 satellites versus OneWeb's roughly 650.
items.title: Sunil Bharti Mittal Prepares Starlink Rival OneWeb Satellite Network

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, the first increase since February 2023, while injecting ₹2.5 lakh crore liquidity into banks. Lending expert Joydeep Gupta explained that higher rates may raise home and personal loan costs over roughly three months for floating-rate borrowers, though new lending need not become harder; attention turns to the December MPC meeting on 2-4 December 2026.
items.title: RBI Raises Repo Rate While Injecting Liquidity

items.summary: According to a person familiar with the matter, Microsoft will not exercise an option that would have more than doubled its existing agreement with AI cloud provider Nscale for computing power at a Texas data center. The Financial Times first reported the news; a potential extension would have been worth tens of billions of dollars for Nscale. Microsoft and Nscale did not respond to comment requests.
items.title: Microsoft declines option to expand Nscale Texas data center deal

items.summary: Google announced it will switch off its Gemini and Search AI features by default on K-12 student accounts worldwide, beginning in the United States, with no date set. The move follows criticism over pushing artificial intelligence into classrooms while schools debate usage. Google framed the change as giving schools more choice, though New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused it of using monopoly power to force AI into public education.
items.title: Google Turns Off AI Tools for School Children By Default

items.summary: Elon Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars on the US midterm elections, but his companies fell after Democrats took both chambers of Congress. In premarket trading, shares of Musk-owned companies came under pressure, with SpaceX falling 3.8% in premarket trading and Tesla slipping 3.6%, as they underperformed the broader market even while equities rallied. The S&P 500 jumped 1.6%. An analysis by The New York Times suggests that Musk contributed $474 million to Republican candidates during the 2026 midterms, including almost $224 million in Texas alone, making him the biggest donor of the election by a considerable margin. Analysts and experts expect greater scrutiny of data-centre projects as Democrats control Congress.
items.title: Musk's Midterm Spending Backfires as Tesla and SpaceX Stocks Fall

items.summary: China's National Development and Reform Commission blocked SoftBank's US$5.4 billion acquisition of engineering group ABB's robotics division, the Swiss firm said on Nov 5. This follows Meta being ordered to unwind its deal with Manus earlier in 2026. The NDRC cited concerns over robotics data flowing overseas for AI training. ABB shares fell 1.1%, while SoftBank shares dropped about 5% before and 6.8% at close.
items.title: China Rejects SoftBank Bid for ABB Robotics Unit

items.summary: Three Orchard Central tenants told by landlord Far East Organization to vacate levels 5 to 12 by end-November have moved to JustCo Place at 160 Orchard Road. Evolve MMA, Helen's and K. STAR Karaoke will occupy the site; Evolve MMA takes a 10,000 sq ft flagship there. Retailers are expected to open progressively from December, with co-living space due in 2027. JustCo Holdings said it has secured retail leasing commitment for 80% of its retail space.
items.title: Orchard Central tenants relocate across road to JustCo Place

items.summary: A Rohini-based Delhi company, which posts as Financersaab (@financersaab2.0), gave its employees iPhone 16 handsets instead of traditional sweets this Diwali and posted a short video on Instagram that went viral. Viewers praised the gesture while joking about job openings. The clip has not been independently verified beyond the company's own post, and the firm did not disclose how many staff received phones or the cost.
items.title: Delhi Firm Gifts iPhone 16 To Staff For Diwali, Internet Asks 'Any Vacancies?'

items.summary: OpenAI shipped image models Flare and Sunburst across ChatGPT, Codex and the API. The release adds animated GIF output, SVG export, markup-guided edits and a complexity parameter with no extra fee. OpenAI states images generate about 50% faster than before, with Flare returning an image in as little as 6 seconds at low quality. Weekly generation rose from more than 3B to more than 4B across ChatGPT and the API, averaging over 500M per day. Token pricing is $30 per million output tokens; OpenAI notes no benchmark scores or per-image cost table for 2.6.
items.title: OpenAI Ships Images 2.6 With GIF and SVG Support

items.summary: The 140th Canton Fair in Guangzhou is closing on November 4 after drawing 32,000 exhibitors. Organizers say the expo centered on robots, AI and green technology: 64% of exhibitors integrated industrial internet and AI into R&D, while new products made up a record 23.2% of exhibits. Customs data shows China's imports and exports of industrial robots, electronic components, computer parts and electrical equipment surged 58.9% year on year, topping 10 trillion yuan ($1.49 trillion) in the first three quarters of 2026. Officials frame the fair as evidence that Chinese trade is running on a brand-new model built around higher-value products and more comprehensive services.
items.title: Canton Fair Marks China's Shift Toward High-Value Trade

items.summary: The Centre told the Supreme Court on Thursday that it is contemplating constituting a committee to revisit the University Grants Commission's notified rules, which were introduced to prevent caste discrimination in educational institutions. The statement was conveyed through Bar and Bench, reported by digital journalist Rohitashwa Ranjan of The Times of India.
items.title: Centre tells Supreme Court it is considering a committee on UGC equity rules

items.summary: Crude futures slipped below $95, with WTI falling under $87 on Thursday morning. The decline lifted sentiment toward companies using oil as a raw material and airlines facing elevated fuel costs. IndiGo shares surged 7% to Rs 5,489 apiece; SpiceJet jumped around 5%. Asian Paints rallied nearly 7%, while Indigo Paints and Berger Paints rose up to 5%. MRF gained more than 4%, Apollo Tyres and Balkrishna Industries jumped over 8%, and oil marketing companies including HPCL, BPCL and IOC rose up to 7%. Analyst June Goh of Sparta Commodities said markets are pricing in a higher likelihood the war will end. Sunny Agrawal of SBI Securities noted that if crude stays below $90-100 per barrel, inflationary pressures could ease for India's economy and equity markets.
items.title: Indian crude-sensitive stocks rally as oil prices fall

items.summary: The Election Commission announced a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in six states and Union territories, including Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim. It directed the chief secretaries to provide adequate manpower so that final rolls are completed by January 21.
items.title: Election Commission Orders Electoral Roll Revision Across Six States and Union Territories

items.summary: A webpage promotes a 90-second video showing the construction of Adora Flora City, described as China's second domestically built large cruise ship. After four years of building, it is scheduled to be officially delivered on Nov. 6 in Shanghai and will begin commercial voyages on Nov. 22, focusing on southern China and Southeast Asia. The vessel has 2,130 cabins and can hold up to 5,232 passengers at full capacity.
items.title: China's Second Domestically Built Large Cruise Ship Set for Delivery

items.summary: A group of military attachés visited a museum in Zunyi, Guizhou Province, to practice calligraphy while learning about the history of the Long March. The foreign guests wrote "Loushan Pass" on Wednesday at a museum displaying Mao Zedong's poems. Loushan Pass was where the Red Army gained its first major victory since the beginning of the Long March in 1935.
items.title: Military Attachés Study Calligraphy and Long March History in Zunyi

items.summary: The 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Foreign Ministers' Meeting was held Wednesday in Beijing. The six member countries reviewed a decade of cooperation and pledged closer ties, with new commitments in areas such as disaster prevention and artificial intelligence.
items.title: Six Nations Pledge Closer Ties at Lancang-Mekong Meeting in Beijing

items.summary: A Beihang University team is designing a conceptual road on the moon, made from crushed stone excavated in situ or sintered there. Professor Li Feng told CGTN that modern roads began as gravel surfaces, so the lunar version could follow suit. The Qinzhidao concept honors an ancient Chinese highway over 2,200 years old. Published January 2026 in the China Journal of Highway and Transport.
items.title: Beihang University Team Designs Concept for China's First Lunar Road

items.summary: Analysts expect the Bank of England to raise rates at its meeting, with Deutsche Bank predicting a split vote in favour of the move. Meanwhile, the FTSE 100 hit a three-month high as markets reacted positively.
items.title: Bank of England Rate Hike and FTSE Record High

items.summary: The French prime minister's office said an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome was diverted to a military base in Évreux after a bomb alert. Flightradar24 reported no aircraft departed Fiumicino Airport in the past 30 minutes and described the plane veering toward France before circling without landing. The incident followed seven European flights searched or diverted two days earlier.
items.title: Aer Lingus Flight Diverted After Bomb Threat in France

items.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage appointed Angus MacIntyre, an RAF wing commander with a 40-year career, as its shadow armed forces minister. In interviews Michel Barnier said the UK could rejoin the single market without joining the euro but free movement would remain non-negotiable.
items.title: UK can avoid euro but must accept free movement to rejoin EU, says former top Brexit negotiator – UK politics live

items.summary: A second buyer, Xyra Group, has made a rescue bid for discount retailer Poundland as it faces collapse with thousands of jobs at risk. London-based Xyra offered to immediately repay £12.5m of the firm's £30m outstanding loan, though doubts remain over its credibility and whether buyers meet Gordon Brothers' tests. US owners Gordon Brothers rejected an earlier Irish bid and urged protection of staff during talks led by Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds.
items.title: Xyra Group Rescues Poundland Amid Collapse Fears

items.summary: The Democrats' sweep in the US midterm elections, which gave them control of the Senate and House, is being read as a win for the global renewable energy industry. Across financial centres worldwide, developers saw their market value climb; Ørsted jumped almost 10% within hours before closing almost 5% higher, while Portugal's EDP Renewables and France's Engie rose more than 3%, Germany's RWE about 1%. The rally comes after the Danish firm lost more than 70% of its market value since Trump returned to office in 2025. Analysts say the shift may reduce regulatory risk, protect solar and wind tax credits, and ease financing for new projects. Brenda Shaffer called it an energy election; Jason Grumet said affordable power is now a priority.
items.title: Midterm victory lifts renewable energy stocks after Trump hostility

items.summary: Protesters across Europe are planning two days of action against datacentres this week with demonstrations taking place in 15 countries. More than 100 groups are joining together for the “Stop Dirty Data Centres” events on Friday and Saturday, calling for a moratorium on large projects citing environmental costs that “we can no longer afford”. Owen Espley, campaign coordinator, said communities across Europe are rising up to demand politicians impose moratoria. Organisers expect attendance ranging from a handful at some gatherings to several hundred at larger ones such as in Brick Lane and Dublin. Groups backing the protests include Friends of the Earth, Greenpeace and Foxglove.
items.title: European Activists Plan Two-Day Datacentre Protests Across 15 Countries

items.summary: A study published in Proceedings of the Zoological Society documents the Rabha community's traditional consumption of the Indian black earth tiger spider (Lyrognathus crotalus), collected from sal forests across western Assam. Researchers Jyotiprakash Boro, Kuldeep Bora, Chandramita Boro and Samir Terdalkar conducted fieldwork between April and June 2025, interviewing 34 community members in Mouman village. The spiders are gathered during three to four days a month before the monsoon, with each trip yielding about 20 to 30 individuals. Collected from burrows near sal trees, they are washed, fried in mustard oil and eaten whole as a seasonal delicacy passed down through generations. Rabha elders describe it as both food and rite of passage, though researchers note the study does not establish its nutritional composition or conservation status.
items.title: Rabha Community's Traditional Tarantula Harvest Documented

items.summary: Carnelian Mutual Fund raised about ₹632 crore in its maiden new fund offer through roughly 30,000 applications. An average ticket size of around ₹2.07 lakh spanned every state, with 45 per cent of applications coming from beyond the top 30 cities and units allotted on November 5, 2026.
items.title: Carnelian Mutual Fund's Maiden Small-Cap NFO Draws ₹632 Crore

items.summary: A plane flying from Dublin to Rome was rerouted to Evreux airbase in France on Thursday (Nov 5) after a bomb threat, the French government said. Quoting Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's office, Reuters reported the Airbus A320 diversion. Flight-tracking site Flightradar24 noted an Aer Lingus aircraft declared an emergency and circled near Paris. The incident followed about 10 European flights targeted by bomb threats on Tuesday.
items.title: Dublin-Rome Flight Diverted After Bomb Threat, France Says

items.summary: Brent crude futures edged up 78 cents, or 0.8 per cent, to $95.40 a barrel as investors weighed the future of the US-Israeli war with Iran following Republican midterm losses this week. UBS's Giovanni Staunovo said prices showed modest recovery while the Middle East situation stays unresolved. Eurasia Group cut its estimate for renewed strikes on Iran to 60 per cent, though it raised odds of a continued standoff and warned volatility could push Brent toward $110 to $125.
items.title: Brent crude rises on Iran war uncertainty after US midterms

items.summary: A speaker argues that recent American elections produced resoundingly moderate outcomes, repudiating both Trump and the extreme Democratic left, while trends in teen mental health are positive. These developments occur as social media usage continues unabated and short video rises further. The speaker concludes these results indicate standard anti-social media polemics are radically incomplete and currently failing in their predictions, though neither trend is guaranteed to continue.
items.title: Moderate election results and rising teen wellbeing challenge social media critiques

items.summary: Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane after refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, which he called an insult to his culture. Australia's Fair Work Commission ruled against him on a late filing. Managing director Elliot Ingram said there was more to the case than toppings.
items.title: Italian Chef Fired Over Pineapple Pizza Refusal Loses Claim

items.summary: An Airbus A320 flying from Dublin to Rome was diverted to Evreux airfield west of Paris after a bomb threat, according to the office of French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu. Tracking websites showed it deviating sharply near Paris before landing safely. The incident follows hoax threats earlier this week that caused diversions and security mobilizations across several European airlines.
items.title: Aer Lingus flight diverted amid bomb threat

items.summary: An article argues that team sports like American football rely heavily on tactical innovation, using the Chicago Bears' Monday Night Football win over Seattle as an example. Head coach Ben Johnson deployed formations and plays that disrupted the Seahawks' defense. The piece contrasts this with individual sports, where such coordinated scheming is less central.
items.title: Sumo's peak optimization mirrors football's technical innovation

items.summary: An Airbus A320 flying from Dublin to Rome was diverted Thursday to France's Evreux airbase after a bomb threat, the French prime minister's office said. It is part of recent threats against European flights; some 10 were targeted Tuesday, closing Warsaw airport briefly and scrambling planes in Rome. No one was injured.
items.title: Bomb Threat Diverts Dublin-Rome Flight to French Base

items.summary: Bob Dylan visited Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican Wednesday during a break between concert dates in Italy, an encounter described by the Vatican as brief. The pope gave Dylan a rosary and received his autobiography Chronicles: Volume One. Spadaro said Dylan wanted to speak privately with Leo for a few minutes.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Welcomes Bob Dylan at Vatican

items.summary: France is bracing for a nationwide strike as hundreds of thousands of protestors are expected on Thursday, involving trade unions, the yellow vest movement, students and workers across sectors. The mobilisation follows lawmakers rejecting the first part of the 2027 budget bill in unified consensus. The government's original proposal will now go before the Senate, with a vote scheduled for 9 December. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez announced more than 70,000 law enforcement officers would be deployed to ensure demonstrations occur peacefully and without incidents. Trade unions condemned what they described as excessive policing amid ongoing debt and deficit concerns ahead of April elections.
items.title: France Prepares for Nationwide Strike Over Austerity Budget

items.summary: As Diwali approaches, Delhi-NCR faces hazardous air while Mumbai stays unhealthy, prompting a surge in persistent coughs across India's largest cities. Doctors explain that the symptoms of smog exposure, seasonal influenza and common colds overlap so closely that self-diagnosis is unreliable. Dr Rommel Tickoo notes the similarity makes identifying causes difficult, while Dr Sagar Srivastava points to shared signs like sore throat and breathlessness. The cough may also linger for weeks due to post-viral airway sensitivity worsened by pollution. Experts advise seeing a clinician if breathlessness, chest pain or fever appear, and recommend flu vaccination as a precaution.
items.title: Delhi and Mumbai doctors weigh pollution cough against flu

items.summary: A ferocious storm last weekend inundated communities across the Southwest, killing at least four people after Clovis, New Mexico received 28.84 inches of rain versus a historical average of just 3.3 inches in September 20. Russ Schumacher of the Colorado Climate Center called the El Niño connection clear and said warmer Pacific waters are priming much of the southern United States for increased winter precipitation, per NOAA's outlook. Michael A. Crimmins of the University of Arizona noted such an event could occur without El Niño but would be far less likely. Any added rainfall might ease drought strain on Lake Powell and Lake Mead, though Schumacher said it cannot reverse their decline.
items.title: El Niño storms flood Southwest and may bring wetter winter

items.summary: Researchers at South Korea's Dongguk University built an anode-free all-solid-state battery prototype that delivered a volumetric energy density of 235.13 Wh/L, the researchers reported. The design uses an ultrathin tin/carbon interlayer on a copper current collector to guide lithium deposition and includes prelithiation to offset early losses. Lead author Hyun-Suk Kim said the approach could support thin-film batteries for wearable electronics and scalable industrial power.
items.title: Korean Researchers Prototype High-Density All-Solid-State Battery

items.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that the 24-hour deadline to produce a detained person before a magistrate begins at custody, not formal arrest. A bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar held treating detention and formal arrest as separate events is constitutionally unsustainable. Petitioners alleged authorities delayed recording their arrest on September 30, 2025, after detaining them on September 29, 2025, to circumvent the deadline under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act. The court also directed magistrates to record when liberty was curtailed and release anyone held beyond 24 hours without production.
items.title: Supreme Court Sets Detention Start for 24-Hour Bail Rule

items.summary: Nippon Steel Kowa Real Estate, Sumitomo Life Insurance and Obayashi Corp. are implementing a green hydrogen project at Shinagawa Intercity in Tokyo’s Minato ward. It is the first to receive funding under the Tokyo Metropolitan Government’s support program for practical green hydrogen production. Rooftop solar panels generate electricity used to produce hydrogen via electrolysis, which is stored and converted back into power through fuel cells. The companies have not disclosed installed capacities or storage volumes. Separately, they introduced an off-site physical corporate PPA expected to supply about 3 GWh of renewable electricity annually with around 1,200 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions reduction per year.
items.title: Tokyo Companies Test Solar-Powered Hydrogen at Office Complex

items.summary: The Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) will lengthen e-way bill numbers from 12 to 14 digits starting 1 January 2027, as electronic document volumes for goods movement keep rising. GSTN said in an advisory issued on 4 November that current numbering capacity is nearing exhaustion. Finance ministry data presented in the Lok Sabha shows bills generated climbing from 773.9 million in FY22 to 1,419 million in FY26, up nearly 83%. The change is a backend upgrade only; thresholds and compliance rules stay unchanged. Businesses must update systems ahead of the date. Pankaj Dikshit of Cygnet.One called it a necessary technology upgrade to support growth.
items.title: GSTN Extends E-Way Bill Numbers to 14 Digits From January 2027

items.summary: An Airbus airliner flying from Dublin to Rome was rerouted Thursday and escorted by military aircraft after a suspected bomb threat, French authorities said. The plane reached the Evreux airfield west of Paris while France's air force responded quickly. Separately, Bulgaria reported three Ryanair flights faced threats, with one diverted to Plovdiv. About 10 European flights were targeted Tuesday; the UK called them malicious hoax threats.
items.title: Airbus Flight Diverted After Bomb Alert

items.summary: The Queensland Police Union is urging mandatory minimum sentencing for serious assaults on police after an officer was allegedly attacked in Mount Isa, leaving him with a cut jaw. The union president said prison should be the only option. A Griffith University law lecturer argued harsher penalties would not deter offenders and could worsen court efficiency. Sentencing data shows such matters rose from 220 to 360 between financial years ending October 2019 and October 2025, with 48 per cent resulting in imprisonment and 20 per cent wholly suspended.
items.title: Queensland Police Union Pushes Mandatory Sentences After Mount Isa Assault

items.summary: A woman, whose identity was suppressed by Magistrate Clare Stanyer citing an ongoing matter, appeared at the Perth Magistrates Court accused of aggravated stalking with intent to intimidate and demanding property by written threats against WA Greens senator Jordon Steele-John. She is 40 years old and granted bail not contacting him. The allegations relate to workplace misconduct reports; Senator Steele-John denies them, while an external investigation runs.
items.title: Woman Charged With Stalking WA Greens Senator Appears in Court

items.summary: Rahul Matthan, in his book Ex Machina: Essays on a Decade of Tech Policy (Westland), argues that India’s privacy approach should shift from consent to accountability. He notes the country has no formal privacy statute but eight rules under the Information Technology Act, 2000 built around prior permission—a model he calls dead given today’s data volumes and technologies like big data and neural networks. Matthan contends regulators should instead focus on making organisations accountable for how they handle personal data, positioning India as able to leapfrog older frameworks. The piece draws partly on Charles Colman’s scholarship about Samuel Warren’s 1890 Right to Privacy article and its role in LGBTQ+ protections.
items.title: Lawyer Argues India Should Prioritise Data Accountability Over Consent

items.summary: China's Macao Special Administrative Region has ranked first for consecutive years in the China Tourism Academy's ranking for Chinese outbound tourist satisfaction. The article frames green tourism as central to upgrading urban governance and sustainable development rather than mere sightseeing. Three experts weigh in: Wong Seng Fat of the Smart City Alliance Association describes it as an all-for-one model centered on ecological priority, cultural continuity, low-carbon emissions reduction and sustainable operations; Li Xi of City University of Macau cites three dimensions—strategic positioning, national dual-carbon alignment and community operating efficiency; Cui Wenjing notes governance is expanding from individual measures to destination-level management. Achievements include green hotel awards and wetland conservation, though bottlenecks such as limited resources, weak public awareness and incomplete standards remain.
items.title: Macao Leads China in Tourist Satisfaction, Pushes Green Tourism Transition

items.summary: After the Democrats captured both chambers of Congress, analysts weighed what it means for US economic policy while President Donald Trump keeps two years left in office. Markets rebounded after an initial dip as investors took heart from the Democratic victory. Stephen Brown of Capital Economics said the gains do not change much near-term outlook because the party lacks a filibuster-proof Senate majority and Trump holds veto power, which he may use to block legislation. Jacob Funk Kirkegaard warned of two years of gridlock but noted local opposition could still hinder data-center construction and weigh on big-tech valuations. Polling from Pew Research Center found 56% view Trump's tariff policies as mostly negative versus only 20% positive, a sentiment that helped Democrats win in export-heavy states.
items.title: Democrats' midterm win and its uncertain impact on Trump's economic agenda

items.summary: A passenger plane traveling from Dublin, Ireland, to Rome, Italy, was diverted to Evreux Air Base in Normandy after a bomb threat on board. The French prime minister's office told broadcaster BFMTV Thursday that the situation was being monitored in real time by its office. Flight-tracking website Flightradar24 reported the Aer Lingus A320 turning back over southern Paris before heading toward the air base.
items.title: Passenger Plane Diverted After Bomb Threat Reported Onboard

items.summary: BSP chief Mayawati questioned the credibility of electronic voting machines ahead of Uttar Pradesh polls, alleging they were used to influence free and fair voting. Reporting by Press Trust of India carried her claims that a large section of voters want ballot papers restored. She said concerns predate Congress-led governments and now reflect wider public demand.
items.title: Mayawati Challenges EVM Credibility, Calls for Ballot Paper Return

items.summary: Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense issued two brief 'potential danger' warnings for Sharurah governorate in the southwestern Najran region on Thursday via X and its National Early Warning Platform for Emergencies. Minutes later it announced the danger had passed without clarifying its nature or causes, urging residents to keep following instructions and avoid gathering or photographing. The alerts came amid continued Houthi missile and drone attacks; Saudi Arabia has led a coalition against Yemen's Houthis since March 2015 over territory held by them since September 2014.
items.title: Saudi Civil Defense Issues Two Warnings, Then Says Danger Passed

items.summary: The Central government told a Supreme Court bench, led by the Chief Justice of India, that it is considering appointing a committee to review the controversial UGC Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions Regulations. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the issue was being examined so every student feels protected and no section dissatisfied. The court granted more time for guidelines on caste-based discrimination and ragging; the regulations remain stayed.
items.title: Supreme Court Grants Time on UGC Caste Rules

items.summary: Germany's MBDA Deutschland won a contract for its first airborne laser demonstrator, aiming to counter drones and cruise missiles on future Luftwaffe aircraft. India's DRDO seeks an industry partner for a 30kW-class counter-drone laser that completed trials in August 2025, following Operation Sindoor in May 2025. MBDA claims it demonstrated a full system as early as 2012. Lasers engage at light speed and run out of ammunition only when power fails.
items.title: India and Germany Invest in Airborne Laser Weapons Against Drones

items.summary: Hindustan Times reports that Delhi Police informed Municipal Corporation of Delhi officials about unauthorised construction at the three-storey Chawri Bazar building on June 15, but no action was taken. The structure collapsed Thursday morning, killing two people and injuring one. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered an inquiry, registered an FIR against the contractor, suspended two engineers, and said further investigation would reveal the cause.
items.title: Delhi Police Had Warned MCD of Unsafe Building Before Collapse

items.summary: The Centre has modified the Agnipath short-term recruitment scheme, extending a second engagement period for the remaining 75% of first-batch Agniveers who were due discharge with an Rs 11.71 lakh exit package and no pension or ex-servicemen benefits. Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani announced on October 4 that the Union Cabinet approved enrolment as regular personnel subject to selection criteria, describing it as a pathway for all Agniveers into defence forces. The Federal frames this as a course correction after four years, noting fiscal and combat-readiness concerns while flagging unresolved structural reform needs.
items.title: Modi government revises Agnipath scheme after four years of defence reforms debate

items.summary: The Union government told the Supreme Court it is contemplating a committee to revisit the University Grants Commission’s (UGC) 2026 equity regulations, which were notified on January 13 and stayed by the court on January 29. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justice Joymalya Bagchi urged the Centre to ensure the framework protects every student. The petitions mainly challenge Regulation 3(c), arguing it excludes general-category students and lacks a mechanism for false complaints, filed by Rahul Dewan, Mrityunjay Tiwari and Vineet Jindal. Upper-caste groups have protested in Delhi against the rules.
items.title: Supreme Court panel on UGC equity rules

items.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945 that would let licensing authorities immediately suspend manufacturing licences when a drug is declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ). The draft removes show-cause delays, targets five quality parameters—assay, dissolution, related substances, impurities and sterility—and requires Root Cause Analysis before reinstatement. Licences stay open for public feedback for 30 days.
items.title: Health Ministry Proposes Immediate Suspension of Licences for Substandard Drugs

items.summary: The pound rose to its highest level since the June 2016 referendum, according to Bank of England figures. A basket measure against 18 currencies reached an index value of 86.4, where 100 equals 2005 levels. The rise follows political stability and growth ahead of a widely expected interest rate increase on Thursday. Economist Jim O'Neill said people were underestimating the UK's improving momentum.
items.title: Sterling Reaches Highest Level Since Brexit Referendum Amid Expected Rate Rise

items.summary: Cummins India shares fell roughly 15% after the company reported a second-quarter net profit decline of about 19% year-on-year, with margins compressed by 680 basis points. EBITDA margin contracted to 13.9% from 21%, while domestic sales rose 5% and exports grew 2%. The firm cited disciplined execution, price realisation and cost management as it tracked external developments.
items.title: Cummins India Shares Fall After Profit and Margin Slips

items.summary: Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono expressed “immense pain” after Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died the day following a collision between them in a second-division match on Monday. In a club statement released Wednesday, November 4, Owono called it “the most difficult days” of his life and said he faced questions with respect. Spanish media report he could face suspension or court action for negligent homicide. Tenerife declared six days of mourning; matches were postponed across Spain and Europe, with a funeral set in Navahermosa on Saturday, November 7.
items.title: Owono Mourns De Miguel as Tenerife Declares Mourning

items.summary: Kamal Al-Dabary, a 60-year-old former engineering student displaced from al-Mawasi near Khan Yunis, has built homemade wind turbines using scooter motors and salvaged components to generate power. The devices store energy in batteries and provide limited electricity for phones, lights, fans and razors. With solar panels costing nearly $5,000 and Gaza's infrastructure damaged, the invention offers an affordable alternative.
items.title: Displaced Palestinian builds wind turbines for electricity in Gaza

items.summary: Following Democrats' midterm election gains, analysts outline how the party might constrain President Donald Trump's war against Iran. Legislation faces limits: concurrent resolutions are non-binding and binding laws could be vetoed without a two-thirds majority. Investigations into the conflict would be lengthy, though impeachment of figures like Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains possible but unlikely to succeed. The most immediate tool is Congress's power of the purse under Article I, Section 9 of the US Constitution, which requires funding approval for new military spending. However, this could block all military paychecks and risk political backlash, as seen in a similar 2007 attempt over Iraq that President George W. Bush vetoed. Trump acknowledged the war's role in Republican losses but vowed to continue it if needed to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons.
items.title: Democrats Explore Funding Cuts to End Trump's Iran War

items.summary: Pricol reported a 33% YoY rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 85 crore in Q2FY27, from Rs 64 crore. Revenue grew 35% to Rs 1,334 crore. Chairman Vikram Mohan cited operational efficiency and cost discipline as priorities amid changing market conditions. Shares rose around 37% over the past year.
items.title: Pricol Shares Jump After Strong Q2 Profit

items.summary: Bitdefender disclosed a vulnerability dubbed 'GhostMap' that lets an app with no permissions trigger a persistent boot loop on Android devices. The flaw stems from two libraries interpreting ZIP compression differently, causing malformed APKs to bypass size checks and crash the affected process when reading unallocated memory. Researchers demonstrated it using a Pixel 10 running Android 17. Bitdefender reported the issue to Google in August but was classified 'not reproducible.' Remediation options include factory reset or deleting the file via ADB.
items.title: Bitdefender Discloses Android GhostMap Flaw Causing Boot Loops

items.summary: CERT-In, India's cybersecurity agency, issued an advisory identifying a hacking group it calls 'Crafty Falcon' behind AI-driven attacks on non-bank lenders, fintech firms and cryptocurrency exchanges. The agency named four tools—ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI—at least two of which security researchers have linked to China. CERT-In did not say who conducted the breaches or how much money was stolen.
items.title: India's CERT-In Identifies AI-Driven Hacking Group Targeting Financial Firms

items.summary: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), IBM and AMD launched a co-design platform for quantum error correction at IBM's site in Poughkeepsie, New York. The U.S. Department of Energy's Quantum Science Center (QSC) at ORNL and AMD are its inaugural partners. The platform pairs IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 processors with Umbra, QSC's high-performance computing system built on AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs and 5th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs. It lets researchers develop quantum algorithms without building infrastructure themselves. Experiments have run up to 70 logical qubits through 438 difficult operations, a roughly 230-fold jump toward the Genesis Mission's Q Competition target of 100 logical qubits running 100,000 such operations by late 2028.
items.title: ORNL, IBM and AMD Launch Quantum Error Correction Co-Design Platform

items.summary: Hogwarts Legacy received an NVIDIA DLSS 5 upgrade with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering today, bringing lifelike lighting and materials to the game when streamed through GeForce NOW. The update adds detailed visuals while retaining underlying geometry and textures, tuned by Avalanche Software via DLSS 5 developer controls. It also supports DLSS Multi Frame Generation and Ray Reconstruction for enhanced ray-traced graphics. Published by Warner Bros., developed by Avalanche Software under the Portkey Games label, Hogwarts Legacy is an open-world action role-playing game set in the 1800s wizarding world.
items.title: NVIDIA Adds DLSS 5 Support to Hogwarts Legacy on GeForce NOW

items.summary:
Intel is diverting CPU manufacturing capacity from personal computers toward enterprise artificial intelligence infrastructure, confirmed during its recent quarterly earnings call. Rising memory prices and weakening consumer demand are pressuring the PC market, which Intel expects to remain slow through at least the first half of 2027. CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated that demand for Xeon CPUs remains robust despite near-term headwinds across the industry.

visual {
items.title: Intel Redirects Chip Capacity From PCs To AI Infrastructure Amid Industry Slowdown

items.summary: Content management firm Box expanded its partnership with Nvidia on Thursday (Nov 5), unveiling a search engine and an AI workflow builder for Enterprise Advanced customers. The company said the new tool could improve search accuracy by 20 per cent, cut token usage by 90 per cent, and speed up question-answering fourfold.
items.title: Box Expands Nvidia Partnership, Unveils AI Workflow Builder

items.summary: On November 5, IBM, AMD and Oak Ridge National Laboratory launched a joint platform pairing IBM's quantum computers with ORNL's Umbra supercomputer to test methods for detecting and correcting errors in quantum computing. The effort supports the US Department of Energy goal of building a scientifically useful quantum computer by late 2028. IBM said ongoing experiments are roughly 230 times short of that target, while it plans to invest more than $10 billion as it aims to build its first large-scale quantum computer by 2029.
items.title: IBM, AMD and ORNL Launch Quantum Error Correction Platform

items.summary: The podcast asks whether Elon Musk was the US midterms' biggest loser after spending $446m dollars on Republican-aligned political action committees. Democrats won every one of the five Senate races where his America PAC spent most, and hosts Blake Montgomery joined Carter Sherman to discuss what a Democratic wave means for tech.
items.title: Musk's Midterm Spending Called a Poor Investment for Tech

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) implemented a uniform $5 million limit on outstanding positions in rupee-related currency derivatives for domestic clients and foreign portfolio investors across all relevant pairs and exchanges, without requiring underlying exposure. The change aligns with the Reserve Bank of India's revised thresholds announced on 10 October, replacing earlier provisions that had set the limit at $100 million.
items.title: Sebi Aligns Rupee Derivative Limits With RBI Threshold

items.summary: At its developer conference on Thursday, Box unveiled a feature called Box Content Retrieval that embeds Nvidia's Nemotron embedding system into the core of its product. Nvidia VP Kari Briski told TechCrunch she expects queries answered four times faster, with 20% fewer errors and 90% fewer tokens used. The system will reach Enterprise Advance customers early next year.
items.title: Box Integrates Nvidia’s Nemotron Into Agent-First Content Retrieval

items.summary: OpenAI launched the Images 2.6 model, letting users turn photos or text into animated GIFs with adjustable speed (0.5x to 2x) and per-frame edits without video software. It is available in India on free and paid ChatGPT plans.
items.title: OpenAI Unveils ChatGPT’s Images 2.6 for Animated GIFs

items.summary: mm2 Asia (mm2A), the former operator of Cathay Cineplexes, said in a bourse filing on Nov 5 that its proposed restructuring scheme for itself and subsidiary mm2 Entertainment (mm2E) was approved by creditors. The group must now seek court sanction under the Companies Act to proceed. Shares were suspended from trading since Nov 11, 2025, while moratoria protection remains in place until Nov 21, 2026.
items.title: Ex-Cathay Cineplex Operator mm2 Asia Wins Creditor Approval for Restructuring Scheme

items.summary: The page opens with Dhanteras, also called Dhantrayodashi, described as the start of the Diwali festivities and an auspicious time to welcome wealth. It notes that the festival is celebrated with prayers, diyas and buying precious metals, bringing families together in hope. The item then invites readers to share English wishes, quotes and WhatsApp status messages with loved ones to spread festive cheer.
items.title: Dhanteras Wishes Shared Ahead of Diwali

items.summary: Microsoft has declined an option to lease additional computing capacity at its Ward County, Texas data centre for AI start-up Nscale, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Financial Times. The decision may force Nscale to seek new customers or risk losing billions in potential revenue as it prepares for a possible $35 billion IPO this year.
items.title: Microsoft Passes on Expanding Nscale Texas Deal

items.summary: On November 4, election-related queries dominated Google's top searches in the United States, with “Alaska Senate race” leading and “Habibi meaning” reaching the top 10. The term gained attention after newly elected Democratic Senator Abdul El-Sayed used it during his victory speech, addressing Vice President JD Vance as “habibi.” Democrats also made gains, holding at least 54 of 100 Senate seats and flipping at least 30 House seats for a total of 240. Source: Deccan Chronicle.
items.title: Google Search Trends Follow US Midterm Election Results

items.summary: The Students Federation of India (SFI), the student wing of the CPM, lodged a complaint with President Droupadi Murmu against Keralam Governor O.P. Mathur over his Instagram handle "ommathurbjp." SFI Thiruvananthapuram district secretary Nandan M.A. stated that associating the constitutional office with a political party violates neutrality and could erode public trust in institutions.
items.title: SFI Complaint Against BJP Tag on Kerala Governor's Instagram Handle

items.summary: The Bank of England raised interest rates on Nov 5, the first increase in over three years, voting 8-1 to lift rates to 4% from 3.75%. Governor Andrew Bailey said at least one more rise was likely if a Middle East conflict continued, though he warned it would not be inevitable or necessarily final. British inflation is projected to reach around 5% by mid-2027, well above the central bank's target. The Bank also revised up growth forecasts for 2026 and 2027 while projecting inflation peaking at an average of 4.8% in early 2027 under its central scenario.
items.title: Bank of England Raises Interest Rates for First Time Since 2023

items.summary: Meta has joined Google and Microsoft by offering voluntary exit options (VEOs) to staff in France, with a November 5 application deadline. According to La Lettre, roughly 100 of the company's ~300 French employees may be affected. Unlike its rivals' individual offers, Meta uses RCC, a collective contractual termination procedure under French labour law. Participants receive about 2.15 months' salary per year of service plus 10 months of paid leave at 80% gross pay. The move follows April layoffs of ~8,000 roles (~10%) and May reassignments of ~7,000 staff to AI-linked functions, alongside projected capital expenditure between $135 billion and $145 billion in 2026.
items.title: Meta Extends Voluntary Exit Program in France Amid AI-Driven Cuts

items.summary: HRL Laboratories, an IBM company, has developed a new inertial measurement unit (IMU) using micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) sensors to provide uninterruptible navigation as an alternative to satellite-based global positioning system (GPS), which can be disrupted by tall buildings, the deep ocean, or electronic interference. The device uses dead reckoning and is about the size of a soup can, making it suitable for lightweight vehicles like aerial drones. Its key innovation is AutoCal, a self-calibrating system that solves bias drift to enable indefinite navigation use. HRL aims to shrink the IMU further toward hockey-puck size and expects production to begin in 2027.
items.title: HRL Develops GPS-Rivaling MEMS Inertial Navigation System

items.summary: In a VoxDevTalks episode, Michael Peters discusses new research presented at the 2026 STEG conference in Nairobi on service-led economic growth. He argues that many fast-growing developing economies have bypassed industrialisation, with workers moving from agriculture into local consumer services such as retail, hospitality, and small-scale transport rather than factories. New structural estimates suggest productivity gains in these services genuinely raised incomes, but because the services are consumed mainly by wealthy city-dwellers, benefits concentrate among urban households. Peters notes that India's consumer-facing services account for around 20% of private sector employment versus about 12% for manufacturing, and raises open questions about disguised unemployment and South Africa's roughly 30% unemployment rate before suggesting formalisation could help poorer workers.
items.title: Service-led growth may outpace factories in developing economies

items.summary: A study by E. Kipchumba (2026) evaluates the Disability-Inclusive Ultra-Poor Graduation (DIG) programme, a BRAC-run adaptation of an ultra-poor graduation model in four districts of Northern Uganda. The trial covered 185 community clusters and roughly 3,400 households, measuring impacts about 18 months after the programme ended. DIG helped participants with disabilities move from casual paid work into farming, raising named-participant farming participation by about 20 percentage points. However, attitudes did not improve: overall attendance at social events rose 12%, but only among respondents without a disabled household member, and one prejudice measure may have worsened. The author notes the trial cannot isolate what drove attitude change because economic and social components were delivered together (s41). Policy implications include including people with disabilities in such programmes and tackling prejudice directly (s46–s47).
items.title: Uganda graduation programme lifted incomes but not attitudes toward disability

items.summary: In an opinion piece dated Nov 5, 2026, Nathalie Maréchal frames Tuesday's Democratic electoral gains as a rejection of what she calls the tech oligarchy and its allies. She argues that despite these results, technofascism persists and demands accountability through congressional investigations into executive-branch wrongdoing rather than retribution. Maréchal warns that reform will be hamstrung by the White House until 2029, when a new administration takes office in January. She urges structural reforms targeting tech industry power—wealth, data, market concentration—and calls for dismantling Silicon Valley's surveillance-based business models as essential work before broader renewal can follow.
items.title: Columnist Calls for Accountability After Left's Electoral Gains

items.summary: OpenAI announced Thursday it will cover all electricity and infrastructure expenses at future data center campuses it owns and operates, a move aimed at easing growing political backlash against AI data centers and the technology overall.
items.title: OpenAI to Cover Data Center Costs Amid Political Backlash

items.summary: A Europinion report says the delay in Elon Musk's Starlink launch in India comes from pending regulatory and security approvals rather than obstruction by domestic telecom companies, as Musk had alleged. The Indian government called the claim baseless. The report notes both Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel signed distribution agreements, that spectrum pricing was approved but final clearance is still pending, and that over 11,000 villages lacked 4G connectivity as of May 2026.
items.title: Report Questions Musk's Claims of Telecom Blocking Starlink in India

items.summary: Agility Robotics began trading on Nasdaq Thursday, becoming the first publicly listed pure-play humanoid robotics company with active commercial deployments, per the company.
